name: AutoConstrain
tooltip: Generates options using AI technology to automatically dimension and constrain your sketch. Review the proposals and select the one that best suits your needs.

history.note: I couldn't compare this feature because Fusion refuses to run it on this account. AutoConstrain uses AI to propose constraints and dimensions for a sketch. Fusion's API has it as Sketch.autoConstrain with three result options, and only Option 3 can change geometry: it may snap small inaccuracies, such as a nearly-horizontal line. I wrote a case that draws a slightly skewed 40x30 quad, runs AutoConstrain with Option 3, then extrudes it 20 mm. Fusion stopped with 'RuntimeError: 3 : AutoConstrain is not available since user is restricted', so there is no answer key. Fox has no matching command either: sketch.constrain only adds one constraint you choose, and the 'Finish with AutoConstrain' menu item in crates/ui/src/menus.rs has no command behind it. If the probe ever runs, expect it to come back fox-missing. Cases: none.

name: AutoConstrain from datum
tooltip: Place a datum point to align the constraints and dimensions to, then AI technology automatically generates options with dimension and constraints added your sketch. Review the proposals and select the one that best suits your needs.

history.note: AutoConstrain from datum uses AI to add geometric constraints and dimensions to an existing sketch, relative to a datum point you pick. It leaves the geometry where it is, so volume, area, bounding box and face count can't show whether it worked, and no geometry case was built. Fusion's API can run it from a script (Sketch.createAutoConstrainInput, then autoConstrain, with datumPoint, dimensionStrategy, symmetricDimensionStrategy, interLoopDimensionStrategy, linearDiameterDimensionPreference and resultOption), but its result is a constraint state such as isFullyConstrained, not a solid. Fox has no auto-constrain command: the candidates drawing.datum and drawing.datum_target are GD&T drawing annotations, and sketch.constrain only adds one manual constraint at a time. Cases: none.

probe.fix_hint: Fox has no auto-constrain. A fix would add a `sketch.auto_constrain {sketch, datum_point?, dimension_strategy?, symmetric?, result_option?}` command in crates/sketch, with the command registered in crates/engine. It would infer the constraints the geometry already satisfies (coincident, horizontal or vertical, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, equal, symmetric), then add dimensions measured from the datum point until the degrees of freedom reported by sketch.info reach 0, without moving the geometry. tooltip: Constrains two or more arcs, circles, or ellipses to the same center point.

history.note: Tested the Concentric sketch constraint on a chain of three circles, an arc (half disc with line, radius dimension, centre on the line) made concentric with a construction circle, and a circle made concentric with an ellipse. Fox matches Fusion exactly for circles and arcs, but rejects concentric when one curve is an ellipse ("Concentric needs circles or arcs"), so the hole stays off-centre (centre of mass off by (-0.43,-0.26), 5 faces vs 4). Cases: 101-concentric-circle-chain, 102-concentric-arc-to-circle, 103-concentric-circle-to-ellipse.

probe.fix_hint: crates/sketch/src/lib.rs ~line 806: the check for ConstraintKind::Concentric uses `round()`, which only accepts circles and arcs, so it needs to accept CurveKind::Ellipse too. crates/sketch/src/solve.rs ~line 707: K::Concentric gets each centre from self.round(x, id), so it needs a centre lookup that also returns an ellipse's centre point. When the solver moves an ellipse's centre, its major-axis point should move with it (Fusion slides the ellipse across; it does not turn or resize it).

fix.summary:
Fusion's Concentric constraint accepts arcs, circles and ellipses. Fox rejected ellipses with "Concentric needs circles or arcs", so the hole in case 103 stayed off-centre.

What changed:
- **The check** (`crates/sketch/src/lib.rs`): Concentric now accepts ellipses and elliptical arcs. Radius and Diameter still accept only circles and arcs.
- **The solver** (`crates/sketch/src/solve.rs`): Concentric now finds each curve's centre with a new `centre()` lookup, which also returns an ellipse's centre point. An ellipse's major-axis point now moves with its centre when it is "free": no constraint names it, no other curve uses it, and neither point is fixed or held. The solver handles this by solving twice. The first pass ties the free major-axis point to the centre, so the ellipse slides across without turning or resizing, as it does in Fusion. The second pass frees every point so the solve report still gives the right degrees of freedom and free points. If the first pass can't satisfy the constraints, Fox falls back to the all-free solve. A new unit test covers sliding an ellipse onto a circle, a constrained major-axis end, moving a circle onto a fixed ellipse, and rejecting a line.
- **Profiles** (`crates/sketch/src/profile.rs`): a loop made only of same-direction arcs of one ellipse that together cover the whole ellipse becomes a single closed ellipse edge. The extruded plate then has 4 faces, matching Fusion, instead of 5.

New reference cases 101-concentric-circle-chain, 102-concentric-arc-to-circle and 103-concentric-circle-to-ellipse all pass and are in baseline.txt. 101 also survives the edit check and is in edit-baseline.txt; the test reported nothing else to add there.

Checks: `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes with no regressions, the fox-sketch unit tests pass (51), and `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -p fox-sketch --all-targets -D warnings` are clean.

One failure outside this change: in the full `cargo test -p fox-engine` run, `fuzz_features::fuzz_found_bugs` fails (seed 1022 produces an invalid solid). It fails the same way with main's sketch crate, so this change didn't cause it.

name: Curvature
tooltip: Constrains two or more objects to create a smooth, continuous curvature between them (G2 continuity).

history.note: I tested Fusion's Curvature (G2) constraint, which the API calls addSmooth, between a fitted spline and a fixed arc or line. In every case all of the spline's fit points were fixed, so only the spline's end shape could change. Fusion solved all three cases and built the solids. Fox's `sketch.constrain` with type curvature exists but rejects all three with "that constraint conflicts with the others (or over-constrains the sketch)", so the sketch is extruded without the constraint. Fox only satisfies G2 if it is allowed to move the fit points. Separately, Fox gives one face per Bézier piece of the spline, so it reports 9 faces where Fusion has 7. Cases: 104-spline-arc-curvature, 105-spline-line-curvature, 106-spline-arc-same-turn-curvature.
fixer passed the reference test and unit tests; pushed parity/constraintsmooth

probe.summary: I tested Fusion's Curvature (G2) constraint, which the API calls addSmooth, between a fitted spline and a fixed arc or line. In every case all of the spline's fit points were fixed, so only the spline's end shape could change. Fusion solved all three cases and built the solids. Fox's `sketch.constrain` with type curvature exists but rejects all three with "that constraint conflicts with the others (or over-constrains the sketch)", so the sketch is extruded without the constraint. Fox only satisfies G2 if it is allowed to move the fit points. Separately, Fox gives one face per Bézier piece of the spline, so it reports 9 faces where Fusion has 7.
probe.fix_hint: The feature is `sketch.constrain {type: curvature|smooth|g2}` (crates/engine/src/commands.rs ~2510), not the `sketch.blend` candidate: that is the separate Blend Curve tool. The gap is the spline's freedom at the joint. When a Tangent or Curvature constraint is added, `Sketch::add_spline_handle` (crates/sketch/src/freeform.rs ~1150, called from lib.rs `add_constraint`) gives `CurveKind::Spline` only a tangent handle: `end_handle`/`start_handle`, the inner control point of the end piece. The curvature at the end also depends on the end piece's other inner control point (b1), and that comes from interpolating the fit points. So with the fit points fixed, the residual `(ka + kb)` in solve.rs `smooth()` usually can't reach zero, the solve fails, and commands.rs reports a conflict. Fusion turns on both a tangent handle and a curvature handle on a fitted spline, which lets it meet G2 while the fit points stay put. A fix would add a curvature degree of freedom at the constrained end. Options are a second handle point that drives b1 of the end piece, or a scalar curvature/tangent-length parameter. `kind_beziers`/`end_frame` would need to honour it and the solver would need to treat it as a free variable. Secondary: Fox splits a fitted spline into several Bézier faces when extruded (9 faces vs Fusion's 7), which affects face counts. Also, tools/fusion-bridge/FoxBridge/recipe_runner.py now names each fitted-spline fit point `<id>.fit<i>`, so recipes can fix them.

fix.summary:
This replaces my earlier report. The Fit Point Spline fixer has committed, and this branch is now rebased onto their real commit (7cc4ba9, parity/drawspline) instead of the temporary snapshot. My work is one commit on top, 9835112. Merge their PR first; this one then contains only the G2 change.

**Result:** Fusion's Curvature constraint (addSmooth) between a fitted spline and a line or arc now solves in Fox and matches Fusion. Cases 104-spline-arc-curvature, 105-spline-line-curvature and 106-spline-arc-same-turn-curvature build and pass, with the expected face counts (7, 7 and 6). They are added to baseline.txt, after their 198–201. The full reference_parts run passes with no regressions, including 198–201. fox-sketch tests (59), fox-engine sketch unit tests (23) and fox-sketch clippy (-D warnings) are clean. Clippy on fox-engine can't finish locally because its dependencies fox-trace and fox-exchange fail chunks_exact lints in code I didn't touch; that is the local clippy 1.99 being newer than CI's pinned 1.97.

**How Fusion makes a smooth end (measured through the FoxBridge with NurbsCurve3D.getData()):**
- The fit points stay put and the least-energy quintic is refitted.
- The end takes the other curve's direction and curvature: C' = s·t and C'' = κ·s²·n, with no second derivative along the tangent.
- Fusion picks the speed s itself. It is not an energy minimum. From sweeps over directions and curvatures on two- to four-point splines, the rule below reproduces every run to 1e-8 and doesn't depend on which way the curve turns:
  - v = last chord ÷ its parameter share Δt; θ = angle between the end direction and that chord; F = (3 − cos θ)/2.
  - With no curvature, s₀ = 1.44·F·v.
  - Above a threshold, s³|κ| = C, where C = F·v²·max(F²/2, sin θ/Δt).
  - Below the threshold, s follows the tangent line from (0, s₀) to that curve.

**Changes:**
- **Curvature handles:** `CurveKind::Spline` gains optional `start_curvature` / `end_curvature` points. They are serde-optional, so old files load. The curvature is read from the handle's offset across the end tangent, like a point on a parabola, so any curvature is reachable. A Curvature constraint adds one beside the tangent handle.
- **Smooth ends in the fit:** `quintic::End::Smooth` and `Quintic::fit_ends` add the C' and C'' rows. `Quintic::fit` now calls `fit_ends`. The speed rule and handle geometry live in a new file, `smoothend.rs`.
- **Exact end frames:** a spline's end tangent and curvature now come from the quintic itself (`spline_end_frame`), not from its cubic pieces, whose curvature at the end is only approximate (0.235 against a true 0.2 in one test). The solver therefore meets the true curvature.
- **No spurious freedom:** a new implicit solver equation (`Eqn::HandleReach`) holds the handle slides that don't change the curve. A smooth end with fixed fit points now reports 0 DOF.
- **Handles kept through edits:** trim, break, extend, transform, point merge and the scene's handle lines all carry the new handles.
- **Tests:**
  - Speeds match Fusion to 2e-4 for the two-point line and to 2e-3 for the c104 geometry (`speeds_match_fusion`).
  - Constrained poles match Fusion to 1e-5 (`smooth_ends_match_fusion`).
  - A full constraint-path test on the c104 geometry passes.
  - With the constraint on the spline's start rather than its end, the volume is within 0.002% of Fusion's.

The B-rep edge is still built from cubic pieces that match position and tangent only, so the solid's curvature at the joint is close rather than exact. Volumes still match Fusion to within 0.02%.

name: Fix/UnFix
tooltip: Locks the size and location of a point or object.

history.note: Fix/UnFix locks sketch geometry so the solver can't move it. Fox's sketch.constrain type=fix matches Fusion for a fixed point: a rectangle grows away from its fixed corner and measures the same. Fox can't fix a curve, though: fixing a line or a circle fails with "'fix' needs 1 point(s)". The geometry then moves when it's solved: the slanted line shifts, and the circle radii average to 8 instead of c2 taking c1's fixed r10. Cases: 111-fix-point-rectangle, 112-fix-line-rotated-rectangle, 113-fix-circle-equal.

probe.fix_hint: In crates/engine/src/commands.rs, fn constrain, the "fix" arm (around line 2468) only accepts `points`. Make it accept `curves` too. For a line, add ConstraintKind::Fix on both endpoints. For a circle or arc, fix the centre and also lock the radius, which needs a new fixed-radius constraint kind in crates/sketch (lib.rs ConstraintKind plus a residual in solve.rs) or a hidden radius dimension; arcs also need their endpoints fixed. fix.summary:
Fox's sketch.constrain type=fix only accepted a single point. Fusion's Fix/UnFix also locks whole curves, so fixing a line or a circle failed with "'fix' needs 1 point(s)".

Changes:
- crates/sketch: a new `ConstraintKind::FixRadius { curve, radius }`, with its residual in solve.rs and validation in lib.rs. Transforms scale it the same way they move a `Fix`. A new `Sketch::fix_curve(curve)` fixes every point that defines a curve (line ends, arc centre and ends, spline and ellipse points) and adds a `FixRadius` for a circle. It skips points that are already fixed and returns the constraints it added. An ellipse's minor radius is a constant in the solver, so fixing its points locks it fully.
- crates/engine: `constrain` accepts `curves` for `fix`. The result keeps `constraint` (the first id) and adds `constraints`, a list of every id added. UnFix means deleting those constraints with sketch.delete. The command's help text is updated.
- crates/ui: the Fix button now also fixes the selected curves, not just the selected points.
- Tests: a sketch solver unit test (fixed line and circle with perpendicular and equal constraints) and an engine test (fix a circle, make another equal to it, delete the fix, then a radius dimension drives both).
- Cases 111, 112 and 113 are added to tests/reference/baseline.txt. They don't need adding to edit-baseline.txt: the test printed no "Now surviving the edit" line for them.

Results: `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes, with no regressions, and so do `fox-sketch` and the `fox-engine` lib tests. `cargo fmt --all` is clean. Clippy is clean for fox-sketch. Run with `--no-deps`, Clippy fails in fox-engine and fox-ui, and without it in fox-exchange, fox-trace and fox-kernel too. Every one of those errors is outside the lines this branch changes: they come from a newer Clippy toolchain (for example `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`) on code already on main, so I left them alone.

I re-checked the fix already committed on this branch (a8a7e49). It still passes, so I made no new changes. The last attempt was only rejected because `cargo test -p fox-kernel --lib` crashes on exit, and main has that same crash.

**Problem:** Fusion's Ellipse tool takes a centre, the end of the first axis, and a third point that the ellipse passes through. - **fox-sketch:** a new function, `Ellipse2::minor_through(center, major, point)`, works out the other radius from where the pick sits relative to the axis: `b = |y'| / sqrt(1 - (x'/a)^2)`. probe.summary: I tested Fit Point Spline (`sketch.spline` in Fox) with four extruded profiles: a 3-point arch, a 5-point wave, unevenly spaced fit points, and a closed spline. All four built in both apps, and all four came out a different shape in Fox. Volume differs by 4.5% to 19%, the bounding box is off by up to 3.3 mm, and Fusion makes one face per spline where Fox makes one per segment. Fox draws the curve through the fit points a different way from Fusion, can't make a smooth closed spline, and never bulges past the end points the way Fusion does in the uneven case (x from -0.88 to 40.88).
probe.fix_hint:
The gap is in crates/sketch/src/lib.rs. `spline_beziers()`, which `kind_beziers()` uses for `CurveKind::Spline`, builds a chain of separate cubic Béziers: Catmull-Rom tangents between points and half-chord tangents at the ends. Every piece becomes its own edge and face, and the shape isn't Fusion's. Fusion's fitted spline, read through `NurbsCurve3D.getData()`, is a single non-periodic degree-5 NURBS. It is flagged rational, but the weights weren't read; the evenly spaced x control points of the arch look consistent with all weights being 1. Its knots are clamped and evenly spaced, with about 5 spans per fit-point gap: the 3-point curve has 10 inner spans and 15 control points, the 4-point curve 15 spans and 20 control points. It looks like a smooth (minimum-energy) fit through the points. The uneven case bulges past the end points (x -0.88 to 40.88), which Fox's half-chord end tangents can't do.

A fix needs to:
(1) build Spline curves as one B-spline edge, so a spline gives one face, not one per Bézier piece. Look at how `kind_beziers` feeds the kernel profile and edge code.
(2) match Fusion's curve through the points: fit a quintic B-spline through the fit points that bends as little as possible, check it against the control points and knots Fusion gives (reproduce them with `sketchFittedSplines.add` plus `geometry.getData()`), then use those control points.
(3) support closed fit point splines, a periodic curve with no corner at the start point. Today, repeating the first point in `sketch.spline` leaves a corner there (and the rebuilt-spline code in fitspline.rs has no closed case). Fusion sets `isClosed` (a periodic spline); Fox needs a `closed` flag on `sketch.spline` or must detect when the first and last points are the same.

To support the closed case I extended recipe_runner.py's `fitted_spline` with `"closed": true`, which sets `isClosed`, and added a None check after `sketchFittedSplines.add`.

fix.summary:
`sketch.spline` drew cubic pieces with Catmull-Rom tangents. Every piece became its own edge and face, the shape didn't match Fusion's, and a spline closed on its first point had a corner there.

**Fusion's curve.** I read Fusion's fitted splines back through the FoxBridge (`sketchFittedSplines.add` + `NurbsCurve3D.getData()`) for the four cases and several probe curves. Fusion builds:
- one quintic B-spline with weights all 1 and five uniform knot spans per gap, clamped when open and periodic when closed;
- the curve that minimises ∫|C'|² + 5/128·|C''|² + 1/125·|C'''|² dt and passes through every fit point;
- with fit point i placed where the running sum of √(chord_cm + 0.22/gaps) reaches it. This depends on absolute size; it was checked across chord ratios, angles and a 10× scale.

The new `fox_sketch::quintic` module reproduces Fusion's poles to about 1e-6 mm and its closed-seam derivative. It uses a banded KKT solve, with a small dense border for the periodic wrap, so it stays linear in the point count; 1,000 points are tested.

**Changes**
- **Drawing:** a fit-point spline is now this quintic, drawn as one Hermite cubic per span and split at the fit points. That stays within 1e-3 mm of the quintic.
- **Closed splines:** a spline whose last point is its first, or `"closed": true` on `sketch.spline`, is periodic with no corner at the start.
- **One edge:** `Seg::Bezier` has a new `chain` id, the same for every piece of one fit-point spline. The kernel joins neighbouring pieces with the same `chain` into one B-spline edge, using `GeomConvert_CompCurveToBSplineCurve`; a new segment kind 5 means "continues the previous edge". Profile loops are rotated so they never start part way along a spline. So a spline gives one face, as in Fusion.
- **Tangent handles** now fix the end tangent inside the fit. Trim, Break and Extend map fit points to their pieces.
- **Sketch bounds** for fit-point splines now use the drawn curve, not the fit points.
- **DXF import** compares fit points against the new curve when deciding whether a SPLINE is a fit-point spline.

**Behaviour change:** a trimmed or extended fit-point spline is refitted through the points it keeps, so its shape moves a little (up to about 1.8 mm in the tests). Before, the kept part stayed exactly the same. Extend also no longer inserts an extra point to hold the old end's tangent. The sketch-crate trim/break/extend tests now check that the shape stays close, not exactly the same. One engine extend test needed a longer target line because the curve now leaves its start more steeply.

**Tests**
- Cases 198–201 pass and are added to baseline.txt. They have no edit check because each script ends with the extrusion. No listed case regressed.
- New unit tests compare against Fusion's numbers: arch poles, fit parameters, closed seam, and handles.
- New engine tests check that a spline extrudes to one face and that a closed spline has 3 faces and no corner.
- `cargo fmt` and clippy are clean on sketch, kernel, model and engine. I had to add `-A clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, because the local Rust is 1.99 and that new lint fails in untouched crates.

**Failures that also happen on main** (I checked each in a temporary main worktree):
- `fuzz_features::fuzz_found_bugs`, seed 1022, which has no splines;
- the fox-kernel lib test binary crashing on exit after all 31 tests pass;
- an occasional `STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION` in the multi-threaded fox-engine lib tests (seen once in about 12 runs on this branch and once in 8 on main).

- **fox-sketch**: a sketch can now hold included 3D curves (`curves3d`: line, 3-point arc, circle or polyline). They share curve ids with the 2D curves, can record the sketch curve they came from, and stay out of profiles and the solver. `sketch.delete` removes them.

- **fox-model** (new `include.rs`):
  - converts edges and sketch curves into 3D curves;
  - keeps them following their source when the model rebuilds, through the existing edge links in `refresh_links` and through source sketches;
  - builds sketch paths through them (`sketch_path` / `path_segs`), now used by sweep paths, pipe, sweep guide rails and loft rails / centre lines. Paths with no 3D curves still go through `open_path` exactly as before.
- **fox-engine**: new command `sketch.include {sketch?, edges?: [{body, edge} | {point}], curves?: [{sketch, curve}], associative?}`.

  - Geometry off the plane stays 3D.
  - Included 3D curves are drawn and pickable in the viewport.
- **fox-ui**: the "Include 3D Geometry" menu entry, previously disabled, now opens an edge-picking form that runs `sketch.include`.
- **Reference cases**: 205 and 206 now call `sketch.include`, as Fusion's script does, and both match expected.json. 205 also survives the 15% extrude edit (the included edge follows the taller box). Added both to baseline.txt and 205 to edit-baseline.txt.
- **Tests**: new tests in `engine/src/tests_include.rs` check:
  - a sweep and a pipe along an included edge, which follow an extrude edit;
  - in-plane edges forming a profile;
  - an included sketch line following a dimension change;
  - include from a later sketch being rejected;
  - deleting an included curve.
  There is also a unit test in `sketch/src/curve3d.rs`.

Checks: `cargo fmt --all` is clean. `cargo clippy -p fox-sketch -p fox-kernel -p fox-model -p fox-engine -p fox-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean only with `-A clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`. The local stable toolchain (1.99) raises that lint in render-gl, trace and exchange, which this change doesn't touch; CI pins 1.97. `reference_parts` passes.

Two failures were seen that this change didn't cause:
- `fuzz_features::fuzz_found_bugs` (seed 1022, chamfer gives an invalid solid) also fails on unmodified main.
- The fox-kernel lib test binary crashes with an access violation after all 31 tests pass. It does the same with the kernel change reverted.

name: Isoparametric Curve
tooltip:
Creates smooth curves along a face in the U or V direction.

Select to create a single curve or a series of curves, select a face, and specify the curve distribution on the face.

history.note: In Fusion, Isoparametric Curve adds sketch curves that follow a face at a constant U or V value. The settings that change the result are the face, isUDirection, and either setSingle(isPhysical, distance), where the distance is a fraction from 0 to 1 or a real length, or setDistributed(quantity). Fox has no command that does this, and none of the suggested candidates (select.all, sketch.arc, sketch.info, sketch.spline) is one. Three cases were built: a single U curve at 0.25, a single V curve 12 mm from the edge, and 3 evenly spaced U curves, each on a box's top face and then extruded. Fusion built all three. The Fox scripts draw the same lines by hand, so their geometry matches Fusion (9000, 7040 and 10000 mm3), but that shows nothing about the feature itself. history.note: Fusion's Midpoint Line (API `SketchLines.addByMidpoint`) mirrors the clicked end through the midpoint, and it also adds a MidPointConstraint that keeps the midpoint point (or the origin, if you snap to it) on the line. Fox's script was written by hand to copy what the tool sends, because the tool has no CLI command, so a UI probe could confirm the result by driving the real tool. fix.summary:
This adds `sketch.project_to_surface`, Fusion's Sketch > Project To Surface. It lays sketch curves onto chosen faces as 3D curves. With `along_vector` it pushes them along a direction (both ways); with `closest_point` it moves each point to the nearest point on the faces. It is a timeline feature (`FeatureKind::ProjectToSurface`). Its curves are stored in `Model::curves3d` and shown in the viewport. A pipe can take the feature as its path and run a round tube along each curve, closed loops included.

- Closed tubes are sewn shut instead of capped, because the two caps sat on top of each other and broke the cut. They sweep with the loop's winding normal as a fixed binormal, so the seam stays on the same side as Fusion's.
- After the cut, faces the tube leaves that cross its seam are split at the seam, as Fusion's faces end there. This gives the along-vector grooves their four faces.
- The projected loop's direction comes from the face normal, even where the loop starts on the face's seam edge.
- Mass properties now integrate faces with free-form edges adaptively, face by face. Default Gauss integration was about 12 mm³ off on the grooved cylinder, depending on where its seam fell. Shapes without such faces are measured exactly as before.

fix.summary:
Adds `sketch.spun_profile {bodies: [id|name], axis: x|y|z|{line}|{axis}|{body,edge}, flip?, centerline?}`, matching Fusion's Sketch > Create > Spun Profile. It draws the outline that bodies sweep through as they turn about an axis. The outline goes on the side of the axis the bodies are on, or the other side when `flip` is set. By default the axis is also added as a construction centre line.

How it works:
- **Kernel** (`cpp/spun.cpp`, `src/spun.rs`; kept from the interrupted fixer's WIP): finds how far the bodies extend along the axis and the stations where corners can occur (vertices and points where edges turn back along the axis). It then cuts planar sections at chosen stations and returns the nearest and farthest distance from the axis for each section face.
- **Model** (new `regen/spun.rs`): splits the axis into stretches between corner stations. Where the number of spans changes inside a stretch, it bisects to find the extra corner. In each stretch it samples the inner and outer reach and fits a line, an arc, or a spline as a fallback. It closes the outline with straight lines across the axis where the material on the two sides doesn't match. It then merges lines that continue each other and arcs on the same circle; an arc that closes on itself becomes a circle, which is how the sphere case gives a single circle. The outline is rebuilt each time the sketch regenerates, so it follows the bodies when they change. Curve ids stay the same when the outline hasn't changed.
- **Sketch** (`spun.rs`, from the WIP): stores the spun profile and its fixed curves.
- **Engine**: the new command traces the outline before committing, so a body that can't be traced gives an error instead of an empty sketch. It is listed in the command registry, and the README has a line for it.

- 243-offset-box-revolve-join and 244-sphere-flip-extrude now pass and are added to `baseline.txt`; 243 also survives the edit check and is added to `edit-baseline.txt`. `reference_parts` passes with no regressions.

probe.fix_hint:
1) Height scale. In crates/sketch/src/text.rs, outline() sets k = height / cap, where cap is the font's OS/2 capital height (1467 units in Arial). Fusion gives the capital H a top of 1.00076 × height in Arial, Calibri and Courier New, and 0.97839 × height in Times New Roman. In Arial that is height / 1464.9 units, so Fox comes out about 0.144% small. One fix is to scale from the measured 'H' glyph height × 1.00076, which matches Arial, Calibri and Courier New. Times New Roman doesn't fit that rule, so check it before committing to it.
2) Text along a path. sketch.text has nothing like Fusion's setAsAlongPath (path curve, above/below, alignment, character spacing) or setAsFitOnPath. It needs a path parameter that lays the glyphs out along the curve.
3) Extrude default. When extrude is given no profiles, it takes every closed region in the sketch, including the glyph counters (the inside of O, A and so on). Fusion's extrude of a text object leaves the counters out. The extrude profile selection in crates/engine needs to treat text as its glyph regions only.
4) Placement conventions, for reference: Fusion puts the text's ink box at the frame corner (no left side bearing) and turns the text about the frame's centre. Fox anchors the pen origin and turns about the anchor. The test scripts adjust `at` for this.
5) Fusion options Fox lacks: horizontal and vertical alignment in the frame, character spacing, bold/italic text style, and horizontal or vertical flip.

fix.summary:
Fusion's sketch Fillet can round the corner between two lines, a line and an arc, or two arcs. Fox's `Sketch::fillet` (crates/sketch/src/edit.rs) only accepted two lines, so 276-line-arc-fillet (a quarter disc with a 5 mm fillet where the bottom line meets the arc) failed with "a sketch fillet needs two lines".

**What changed**
- `Sketch::fillet` now takes any two lines or arcs that meet at an end. It matches the shared end by point id or by position, as before.
- How the centre is found: each curve is moved the fillet radius towards the other one. A line moves sideways; an arc becomes a circle with the same centre and radius R ± r. The fillet centre is where the two moved curves cross. If they cross more than once, it takes the crossing nearest the corner whose touch points fall strictly inside both curves.
- Each curve is then cut back to its touch point. The new arc runs the short way round, facing the corner, and gets the same Tangent and Radius constraints as before.
- Line-to-line fillets come out the same as before: cases 273–275 still match.
- Clear errors are returned when the curves meet tangentially, or when the fillet doesn't fit (too big, or an arc too tight to round on the inside).
- The `sketch.fillet` help text and error message in crates/engine/src/commands.rs now say lines or arcs, and so do the UI tooltip and selection hint.
- Two new unit tests: line-to-arc (checks the centre at (√1200, 5)) and arc-to-arc (checks the centre is 12 mm from one arc's centre and 8 mm from the other's).
- Cases 273–276 are added to tests/reference/baseline.txt, and their directories are committed.

**Not done:** curves that cross rather than share an end, and Fusion's optional pick points ("near"). None of these cases needs them.

**Checks**
- `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes, and all four cases pass.
- None of them gets the edit check, because the extrude is the last command in each script.
- `cargo test -p fox-sketch` and `cargo test -p fox-engine --lib` pass.
- `cargo fmt --all` is clean, and clippy is clean on fox-sketch.

probe.fix_hint: The failure is in crates/sketch/src/edit.rs, `Sketch::offset`. In the `Geo::Arc` branch, an arc whose offset radius is ≤ 0 (`r2 <= EPS`) returns the "swallows an arc" error. Instead, drop that arc from `pieces` and let its neighbouring offset pieces meet each other directly (the existing `meet` corner pass already does this for lines). Repeat until stable, because removing an arc can also make a short line piece reverse or vanish; that piece should be dropped too. Only refuse when the whole chain collapses. This matches Fusion's `isTopologyMatched = false` result. A `topology_matched` flag could keep today's strict error as an option. Separately, `sketch.offset` (commands.rs:1915) has no both-sides option. Two calls do the same job, but a `both_sides` flag would mirror Fusion's dialog. Other changes: I added a sketch entity type `offset` to tools/fusion-bridge/FoxBridge/recipe_runner.py. Its fields are curves, distance (positive = outward for a closed chain, left of travel for an open one), both_sides and topology_matched. fix.summary:
Sketch Offset now handles an inward offset that goes past a fillet radius the way Fusion does with Topology Match off. All four Fusion probe cases (284–287) build and match their expected.json.

**What changed**
- **`Sketch::offset` (`crates/sketch/src/edit.rs`):** when an arc's offset radius is zero or less, the arc is now left out instead of raising "the offset swallows an arc". Its neighbours then meet directly at a sharp corner. Dropping an arc can make a neighbouring piece run backwards between its new corners (a line, or an arc whose sweep flips), so those pieces are dropped too, repeating until nothing changes. The offset is refused only when the whole chain collapses, or when a closed chain turns inside out (its signed area changes sign).
- **`Sketch::offset_matched(curves, distance, topology_matched)`:** new. With `true` it keeps the old strict error; `offset` calls it with `false`.
- **`sketch.offset` command (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`):** takes `topology_matched` (default false) and `both_sides`, which offsets by +d and -d like Fusion's two-sides option. The command help text lists both.

**Scripts and baseline**
- 286's script now uses one offset call with `both_sides: true` instead of two calls.
- 287's script now sets `topology_matched: false`, as its recipe does.
- 284–287 are added to `baseline.txt`. They aren't in `edit-baseline.txt` because the extrude is the last command in each script, so the edit check doesn't run on them.

Fox matches Fusion when the two lines share a vertex: a rectangle corner in both line orders (each distance is measured along its own line) and an acute triangle vertex. probe.fix_hint: crates/sketch/src/edit.rs, Sketch::chamfer, only accepts two lines whose end points coincide. It should work like Fusion: when no ends meet, intersect the two infinite lines (and reject parallel lines), then measure d1 and d2 from that point along each line toward the side being kept. Fusion keeps each line's end farther from the other line by default, or the clicked side. Move each line's near end to its chamfer point (the end nearest the corner, whether that means extending or trimming), then join the two points with the new line. Crossing lines (where the intersection lies inside both lines) need the same treatment: cut away the overshoot beyond the corner. Sketch::fillet has the same shared-end limit. The sketch.chamfer command in crates/engine/src/commands.rs could take optional 'keep' points to choose the side, like the recipe runner does. The existing reference cases 268-apparent-intersection, 271-apparent-intersection-gap and 272-crossing-lines-overshoot hit the same limit.

fix.summary:
Fox's `Sketch::chamfer` and `Sketch::fillet` (crates/sketch/src/edit.rs) only worked on two lines that share an end, so `sketch.chamfer` rejected Fusion's Two Distance chamfer at an apparent intersection with "a sketch chamfer needs two lines that meet at an end".

**Change:** the code that finds the corner moved into one helper, `Sketch::corner`, used by both fillet and chamfer. It still uses the shared end when there is one. When there isn't, it takes the point where the two lines, extended, would meet, and rejects parallel lines. Each line keeps its end farther from that point. Its near end moves to the chamfer or tangent point, which extends or trims the line as needed. This closes a gap like the one in case 291: the lines are extended to (40,0), trimmed back 15 and 20, and joined, giving 10500 mm³ as in Fusion. The same rule cuts away the overshoot where two lines cross.

history.note: Fusion's Align Constraint (root.assemblyConstraints with a geometric relationship) mates B's bottom face flush to A's top face with a 5 mm offset. It moves B only along the face normal, so B goes from z 0..10 to z 15..25 and keeps its in-plane position at x 50..60. Fox has no assembly or align constraint. Its closest command is a planar joint with face origins and offset 5, which gives the same volume, area and face count, but it also snaps B's face centre onto A's face centre. It moves B only along the face normal, so B goes from z 0..10 to z 15..25 and keeps its in-plane position at x 50..60. Fox has no assembly or align constraint. Its closest command is a planar joint with face origins and offset 5, which gives the same volume, area and face count, but it also snaps B's face centre onto A's face centre. That leaves the bbox max at x 40 instead of 60 and the centre of mass at (20, 15) instead of (22.7, 14.2).
probe.fix_hint: Fox has no assembly or align constraint: sketch.constrain is for 2D sketches only, and joint/joint_origin (crates/engine/src/assembly.rs, mates.rs) use Fusion's joint behaviour, which puts the moving origin right on the fixed origin. A fix needs a new 'align' (assembly constraint) command and feature in crates/model/src/assembly.rs, solved in the joint/placement pass. It would take two geometric relationships (face/face for flush, point/point for coincident, axis/axis for concentric) plus offset and flip. It must remove only the degrees of freedom that relationship fixes, moving the component the least amount (for flush, along the shared normal) and leaving its other position as it was. A planar joint snaps the face centres together, which is the gap this case shows.

fix.summary:
Fusion's Align Constraint makes faces flush, axes concentric or points coincident. It moves the component only along what that relation fixes and leaves the rest of its position as it was. Fox only had joints, which snap the moving origin onto the fixed one. So the planar-joint stand-in for 296-flush-face-offset moved B's face centre onto A's, which put bbox max x at 40 instead of 60 and the centre of mass in the wrong place.

What changed:
- **New command `align`** (crates/engine/src/align.rs, help entry in commands.rs, dispatched after subassembly). It takes `moving_geometry` and `fixed_geometry`, each a face, edge, point or saved joint origin. The components default to the ones those geometries are on; `fixed: null` means the world. It also takes `relation` (auto, flush, coincident or concentric), `offset` (an expression), `flip` and `name`.
- **New feature `FeatureKind::AlignConstraint`** (crates/model/src/lib.rs, appended). It has a type name, dependencies on saved origins, an expression hook for the offset, and blocks deleting a component it uses.
- **Solver: `assembly::align_transform`.**
  - Flush turns the moving plane about its own centre, by the smallest rotation, until its normal opposes the fixed one (or matches it with flip). It then slides the plane along the fixed normal to the offset.
  - Concentric turns the axis parallel and slides it across onto the fixed axis, keeping its position along the axis. It rejects a non-zero offset.
  - Coincident moves point onto point, with the offset along the fixed Z.
  - Auto picks flush for two flat faces, concentric for two axes, and coincident otherwise.
- **Regeneration** (regen/assemble.rs, dispatched from extra.rs). It resolves the geometry with the existing joint frames and moves the component and its rigid group through `move_component`, as joints do. A grounded moving component is an error.
- **Smaller changes:** sub-assembly inserts suppress align constraints when they compute free positions, and the UI timeline shows an icon for the new feature.
- **Case script:** 296-flush-face-offset/part.jsonl now calls `align` with flush and offset 5, and the case is added to baseline.txt. It builds with `box`, not an extrusion, so the edit check skips it and edit-baseline.txt is unchanged.
- **Tests:** a model unit test for the solver, and an engine test for flush with offset, editing the offset, concentric pin-into-hole, and rejecting a component aligned to itself.

`reference_parts` passes with no regressions, and the engine and model unit tests pass. One existing test, `fuzz_found_bugs` (a chamfer step, seed 1022), fails; it fails the same way on main without these changes. Clippy is clean on fox-model, fox-engine and fox-ui. To get it to run, I had to allow `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`: only Rust 1.99 is installed here (CI pins 1.97), and that newer lint fails in fox-exchange, fox-render-gl and fox-trace, which this change doesn't touch.

Fox has no assembly or angle constraint command (no assemblyConstraints equivalent, only joints), so it can't express this. part.jsonl uses the closest Fox tool instead: a revolute joint on the hinge with a flip and a rotation of -150°. probe.fix_hint: Fox needs assembly constraints alongside joints. The joint commands are in crates/engine/src/assembly.rs, with joint_origin, rigid_group and motion_link in crates/engine/src/mates.rs. The model types are in crates/model/src/assembly.rs, where FeatureKind::Joint and JointKind are defined. Add an assembly constraint feature (e.g. "assembly.constrain") that takes a set of geometric relationships between a moving and a fixed component. Each relationship is a face, edge or point pair of type mate, flush, parallel, angle, distance and so on, with a value and a flip. Fusion's API stores these as AssemblyConstraintInput.geometricRelationships.add(a, b, isFlipped, value). The feature needs to solve for the moving component's transform. For the angle relationship, rotate the moving component so the angle between the two face normals equals the value, keeping the other relationships (here the edge-to-edge hinge) satisfied, and choose the solution branch the way Fusion does. Fusion puts the plate at 150° fold-over, not 30° outward. The Fox equivalent in this case is a revolute joint with flip=true and rotation=-150°.

Creates a As-Built Constraint relationship between two components in their current position and defines their relative motion.

Select two components to create an assembly constraint between, then position the constraint snap and specify the joint motion type. Optionally, specify motion limits and preview motion.

history.note: I built three cases, each with a grounded 20x20x10 base and a 30x5x5 arm on top of it, joined at the base corner (20,0,10). history.note: Fusion's Center Constraint is an assembly constraint that centres one component between two faces of another. probe.fix_hint: Fox has only joints (the `joint` command in crates/engine, with planar, slider and other kinds). Every joint snaps one origin onto another, so nothing can constrain only the distance along a normal. A fix needs an assembly-constraint command (for example `constraint.center {moving, moving_faces: [f1, f2] | entity, fixed, fixed_faces: [f1, f2]}`), with siblings for align/flush and angle (AlignConstraintCmd and AngleConstraintCmd are the same gap). It should work out the fixed midplane between the two faces of the fixed component and the moving component's midplane (or chosen entity). Then it should move the moving component along the plane normal by the signed distance between them, keep the in-plane position and orientation (minimal motion), and store it as a parametric relationship that re-solves when the parts change.

fix.summary:
Fox now has Fusion's Center Constraint, and case 301-block-centered-in-channel builds and matches Fusion. Its centre of mass comes out at [25, 9.0385, 5], the same as Fusion's.

**What was wrong:** Fox only had joints, and every joint snaps one origin onto another. The closest stand-in, a planar joint, centred the block in x but also pulled it onto the slot centre in y.

**What changed:**
- **New feature `PlaneConstraint`** (`crates/model`). Each side is either one plane or the midplane between two parallel planes. A plane can be a face, a construction plane or an origin plane.
- **How it solves** (`regen/assemble.rs`). The moving component turns the least it needs to so the two planes are parallel (no turn if they already are). It then moves along the fixed plane's normal by the signed gap plus an optional `offset`. Where it sits within the plane stays the same.
- **Behaviour.** It re-solves whenever the timeline regenerates, so it follows changes to the parts. It goes through the same component move as joints, so rigid groups and saved joint origins move with it. It refuses to move a grounded component or one constrained to itself, and you can't delete a component it uses. Construction planes it references are listed as dependencies, and its `offset` is a normal expression.
- **New command** `constraint.center {moving?, moving_faces: [1 or 2 faces/planes], fixed?, fixed_faces: [1 or 2], offset?, name?}`. If `moving` or `fixed` is left out, it uses the component the first picked face belongs to. The command is in the command list, and the feature has a UI icon.
- **The case's `part.jsonl`** now calls `constraint.center` with the block's two x faces and the channel's two inner faces instead of the planar joint.
- **New engine test** (`tests_assembly.rs`). It checks that the block is centred while y and z stay put, that it re-solves when a parameter widens a wall, that `offset` works, and that a grounded component can't be moved.
- **Baselines:** the case is added to `baseline.txt` and `edit-baseline.txt`.

**Checks:** `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes with no regressions. The fox-model and fox-engine unit tests pass, and `cargo fmt --all` was run. `fuzz_features::fuzz_found_bugs` fails at seed 1022 (fillet/chamfer on a plain extruded body), but it fails the same way on main's code, so this change didn't cause it.

The align/flush and angle constraints (AlignConstraintCmd, AngleConstraintCmd) aren't added yet. The feature already takes one plane per side, so a flush or align command can reuse it.

probe.summary: Constrain Components (Fusion's `root.assemblyConstraints` with a `GeometricRelationships` set) places a free component from one or more pairs of entities: face, edge or vertex mates, flipped or not, each with an offset or an angle. Fusion built all three cases from fusion.py, and expected.json was written for each. Fox has no assembly-constraint command; the only near equivalent is `joint`. probe.fix_hint:
Fox needs an assembly-constraint command, e.g. `assembly.constrain {moving, fixed?, relationships: [{a: face|edge|vertex ref, b: ref, mate: bool, flip?: bool, value: length|angle}]}`. It would be a timeline feature in crates/engine/src/mates.rs (next to rigid groups and contact sets), with dispatch in crates/engine/src/assembly.rs and help text in commands.rs. - Mates make plane-on-plane, edge-axis (concentric) and point-to-point coincidences.
- By default the two entities face opposite ways; flip makes them face the same way.

Fusion's Joint, as built through the API, lines up the two joint origins' Z axes in the same direction and turns them to face each other only when isFlipped is set. Offset, slide and rotation direction otherwise agree: the revolute case, with Fox's flip removed, gives Fusion's numbers.
probe.fix_hint:
The gap is in crates/model/src/assembly.rs, joint_transform. Its line `let mate = if flip { IDENTITY } else { from_rotation_x(PI) }` gives the reverse of Fusion's Joint. Fusion's default is the identity mate: the moving origin's Z, X and Y are lined up with the fixed origin's. isFlipped adds the half turn. The fix is to swap the two branches (`if flip { from_rotation_x(PI) } else { IDENTITY }`), or to invert `flip` where the `joint` command is parsed in crates/engine/src/mates.rs.

None of the existing reference cases hit this path. The ones that use Fusion's Joint API (298–311 and 315–317) all use as-built joints, which return early before the mate. 296–297 and 312–314 use assembly constraints (Constrain Components / Align) and also run through the `joint` command. They depend on the opposite (face-to-face) default and use isFlipped as written now. If Fox maps those to `joint`, keep that behaviour on their path, e.g. as a separate default, rather than changing it for all joints.

I checked these Fusion conventions directly. A planar face's joint Z is its outward normal, and its X is the world X projected onto the face. A vertex origin from createByPoint uses the component's +Z and +X. Offset runs along the fixed origin's Z. Driven rotation is counter-clockwise about the fixed Z, which Fox already does. Two things are still unchecked because the boxes in these cases are symmetric: whether isFlipped turns about X or Y, and how `angle` combines with flip. A follow-up case with an off-centre origin should pin those down.

fix.summary:
I fixed the joint direction, and all four new joint cases now match Fusion. `reference_parts` passes, and no case in the baselines regressed.

**The problem:** Fox had the joint's default direction backwards. In Fusion, an unflipped joint lines up the moving origin's Z, X and Y with the fixed origin's; turning `isFlipped` on adds a half turn about X so the two Z axes face each other. Fox faced them by default and lined them up only when flipped. So every joint that wasn't "as built" put the moving part on the wrong side of the joint plane: case 325 measured z 13..17 in Fox against 9..13 in Fusion.

**What changed:**
- **The fix:** in `joint_transform` (`crates/model/src/assembly.rs`) I swapped the two branches. Unflipped now keeps the axes as they are; flipped adds the half turn about X. Joints marked "as built" return before this line, so they are unchanged.
- **Unit tests:** four engine test joints assumed the old face-to-face default (in `tests.rs` and `tests_assembly.rs`). I added `"flip": true` to each so they keep testing the same arm-on-base placement. The model test `mating_puts_origins_together_facing` now checks both the unflipped and flipped results.
- **Reference cases:** I added cases 325–328 (rigid with an offset, rigid flipped and turned 90°, revolute on a corner, slider driven 5 mm) to `baseline.txt` and `edit-baseline.txt`.
- **Script comment:** I corrected the comment in 325's `part.jsonl`, which said "Z axes facing … z 13..17"; Fusion measured 9..13. `fusion.py` still has the old comment.

**Behaviour change:** any existing Fox design or script with an unflipped, not-as-built joint will now place its moving part on the other side of the joint plane. None of the other reference cases call the `joint` command, so none of them changed.

**Two things I couldn't clear:**
- **Fuzz test:** `fuzz_found_bugs` in `fox-engine` fails at seed 1022, which is a chamfer leaving an invalid solid. That fuzzer never creates joints, so this change can't be the cause. I didn't run it on main to confirm.
- **Clippy:** `cargo clippy -D warnings` stops on a newer lint, `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`, in `fox-kernel` (and `fox-exchange` also fails to compile), neither of which I touched. With only that lint allowed, `fox-model` and `fox-engine` come back clean.

**Still open:** the cases use symmetric boxes, so it's still unchecked whether Fusion's flip turns about X or Y, and how the angle combines with a flip. A follow-up case with an off-centre origin would settle both.

The third case is a cylindrical joint on cylindrical faces with a 5 mm slide and 90° turn, and it mismatches. Fusion uses +Z as the Z axis for both cylinder faces, so the plate ends at z 13..17 with its long end at +Y. Fox uses -Z for the pin's face, so the plate ends at z 3..7 with its long end at -Y.
probe.fix_hint: Fox gets the wrong Z axis for a joint on a cylindrical face. face_frame in crates/model/src/assembly.rs (Cylinder branch) uses FaceInfo.normal as the axis. That value is the raw OCC gp_Cylinder axis from kernel.cpp faces() (around line 619, GeomAbs_Cylinder), and it doesn't take face orientation or the extrusion direction into account. For the pin made by extruding a sketch circle +Z it comes out -Z. Fusion reports +Z as the axis (and joint Z) for both the boss and the hole, which were both extruded +Z. Point the cylinder axis the way Fusion does, along the extrusion direction (+Z here), either in face_frame or by canonicalising the axis direction in the kernel. Then slide and rotation run along +Z, as in Fusion. Separately, edge picks by point are ambiguous where a circle meets OCC's straight seam edge; Fusion cylinders have no seam edge. That may be worth handling in edge resolution.

fix.summary:
All three Joint Constraint cases now pass: 322, 323 and 324. Only the cylindrical joint (324) was wrong before.

**What was wrong:** A joint on a cylindrical face takes its Z axis from the cylinder's axis as OpenCASCADE reports it. Which way that axis points depends on how the surface was built. For an extruded pin it came out -Z, but the hole the pin sits in came out +Z. Fusion uses +Z for both, so in Fox the 5 mm slide and the 90° turn went the opposite way to Fusion's.

**The fix:** In `face_frame` (`crates/model/src/assembly.rs`), the cylinder branch now always points the axis the same way: +Z, or +Y if the axis is level, or +X if it runs along X. So the same cylinder always gives the same joint axis. This only affects joints on cylindrical faces. Only these three reference cases use joints, and none of the existing `fox-model` unit tests changed. The editor's joint preview (`scene.rs`) and the joint-move dialog (`ui/dialogs/manip.rs`) also call `face_frame`, so they pick up the change.

**Checks:**
- `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts`: both tests pass and nothing regressed. Cases 322–324 are added to `baseline.txt` and `edit-baseline.txt`.
- `cargo test -p fox-model`: 100 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all`: run.
- `cargo clippy -p fox-model --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails on errors that were already in the code: 15 `clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` errors in other `fox-model` files and 10 in `fox-kernel`. That lint is new in the current toolchain, and none of the errors are in `assembly.rs`. With only that lint allowed, clippy is clean.

**Not handled:** the probe's side note. Picking an edge by a point where a circle meets OpenCASCADE's straight seam edge can pick the seam instead of the circle; Fusion cylinders have no seam edge. None of these cases needs that changed.

fix.summary:
For conical and toroidal faces, `face_infos()` in `crates/kernel/cpp/kernel.cpp` set only `kind` and left origin, normal and radius at zero. Because the stored normal was zero, `FaceRef::resolve` skipped every curved face at regen (|align| < 0.999). Cones now report `Location()`, `Axis().Direction()` and `RefRadius()`, and tori report `Location()`, `Axis().Direction()` and `MajorRadius()`, the same way cylinders already did. The change also adds the `gp_Cone` and `gp_Torus` includes. It touches only the C++ kernel.

  - `{axis: id}`;
  - `{point}`, which looks for a body edge first and, if none is there, takes the nearest sketch line (new `sketch_line_at`).

probe.fix_hint: The bug is in crates/model/src/regen/extra.rs, in `plane_by`, in the `PlaneDef::Midplane` branch. When the two planes aren't parallel, Fox flips `nb` so that na·nb ≥ 0 and uses `na + nb` as the normal. With two body faces meeting at a convex edge (outward normals +x and +z), that gives the outside plane x+z=60, which only touches the box. Fusion uses the plane that lies between the two faces (x−z=20), with normal na−nb. To fix it, when a and b are body faces, pick the 45° plane that puts the two faces (e.g. their centroids or sample points) on opposite sides. Keep the current choice for construction or origin planes, which already matches Fusion (the two-origin-planes case). For reference, I added a `midplane` method to `op_construction_plane` in tools/fusion-bridge/FoxBridge/recipe_runner.py. It calls `setByTwoPlanes(a, b)`.

fix.summary:
Fox's midplane picked the wrong one of the two 45° planes when given two body faces that meet at an edge. All 4 midplane reference cases (344–347) now pass. I added them to `tests/reference/baseline.txt`, and `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes with no regressions.

**What was wrong:** In `plane_by`, Fox flipped one normal so the two normals pointed roughly the same way, then used their sum. For the x=40 face and the top face of a box, that gives the plane outside the box, which only touches it, so the split did nothing. Fusion uses the plane that runs through the box between the two faces.

**What changed:** In `crates/model/src/regen/extra.rs`, when both inputs are body faces, Fox now builds both candidate planes through the line where the faces meet. probe.fix_hint: Fox's `Plane::XZ` in crates/kernel/src/lib.rs:53 has x=+X and y=+Z, so its normal is X×Z = -Y. Fusion's `xZConstructionPlane.geometry.normal` is (0,1,0) (uDirection is +Z), so Fusion offsets from XZ along +Y. `FeatureKind::ConstructionPlane` in crates/model/src/regen.rs:736 calls `resolve_plane(base).offset(d)`, which takes `PlaneRef::Origin{Xz}` → `OriginPlane::Xz.plane()` (crates/model/src/lib.rs:294), so Fox moves the plane toward -Y. The fix: for an XZ base, offset along +Y. Either give the XZ origin plane a +Y normal (Fusion's sketch frame on XZ is x=+X, y=-Z, normal +Y), which also affects sketches, mirror, split and anything else that uses "xz", or flip the sign only for a ConstructionPlane offset from Origin Xz. crates/engine/src/tests_more.rs:153 (`plane.offset` xz -10) may encode the current sign and need updating. The other offset bases (planar faces in either direction, YZ, XY) already match.

fix.summary:
Offset Plane now moves a plane offset from the XZ origin plane toward +Y, which is what Fusion does. Before this, a +15 offset from XZ ended up at y = -15 in Fox, so case 348 mirrored the box to the wrong side. All four new cases now match Fusion, and no case already in the baselines got worse.

**Cause:** Fox's XZ origin plane (`Plane::XZ`) has X to the right and Z up, so its normal points toward -Y. In Fusion, the XZ plane's normal points toward +Y. `FeatureKind::ConstructionPlane` moved the plane along the base plane's normal, so offsets from XZ went the wrong way.

**Fix:** I kept the change narrow:
- **Model:** a new `OriginPlane::offset_sign()` returns -1 for XZ and +1 for the other planes. The construction-plane regen step in `crates/model/src/regen.rs` multiplies the offset by it.
- **Sketch frame unchanged:** sketches, mirror, split and everything else that uses "xz" behave as before, and so do sketches drawn on the offset plane.
- **UI:** the drag arrow in the Offset Plane dialog (`crates/ui/src/dialogs.rs`) uses the same sign, so dragging it moves the plane the way the arrow points.

**Tests:**
- `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes. Cases 348–351 are added to `baseline.txt`, and 348–350 to `edit-baseline.txt`, as the test asked.
- Two unit tests offset from XZ with the old sign. I changed their signs so the plane ends up where they intended: `rib_grows_to_the_floor` now uses offset +10 for y = 10, and `cylinder_and_square` uses -30 for y = -30. The full `fox-model` and `fox-engine` lib test suites pass.
- `cargo fmt` is clean.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` fails before it reaches my crates. A new Clippy lint (`chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`) flags code in crates this change doesn't touch (`fox-render-gl`, `fox-exchange`, `fox-trace`). With that one lint allowed, `fox-model`, `fox-engine` and `fox-ui` are clean.

fix.summary:
Fox can now make Fusion's Perpendicular Plane, and all four reference cases (352–355) match Fusion's measurements. `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes with no regressions, and `cargo test -p fox-model` passes.

**New command option.** `plane` takes `method: "perpendicular"` with these options:
- `plane`: the base, either a construction plane or a planar face.
- `through` (optional): a point the new plane passes through.
- `distance` (optional): how far to move the plane when there's no `through` point.
- `direction` (optional): `u` (the default) or `v`.

**How the plane is placed.** Its normal is the base's in-plane U direction, or V when `direction` is `v`, so the new plane contains the base's normal. With a `through` point the plane passes through it and `distance` is ignored, as in Fusion. Without one, it starts at the base's origin and moves `distance` along its own normal. On the XZ origin plane, U runs along -X to match what the probe measured in Fusion. No case tests that, and none tests a face base without a `through` point either, because Fusion picks that start point itself.

The code is the new `PlaneDef::Perpendicular` in `construct.rs` (it tracks the base plane and point and treats `distance` as an expression), its build step in `regen/extra.rs`, and the command parsing in `features.rs` plus the help text in `commands.rs`.

**Split body change.** Cases 352–354 split the prism exactly along an existing face. Fox used to leave the new cut face and the old face as two side-by-side faces in the same plane, giving 13 faces where Fusion has 12. Split body now merges such faces in the pieces. It only does this when the original body had no same-plane neighbouring faces of its own, so faces a user split on purpose stay split.

**Baselines.** I added the four cases to `baseline.txt` and `edit-baseline.txt` and committed their folders, which were untracked. The test also lists many other cases as "now passing"; those already pass on main because its baseline is out of date, so I left them out.

**Checks.** `cargo fmt` is clean. Clippy with `-D warnings` fails before it reaches the changed crates, on a new lint (`chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`) in `fox-exchange` and `fox-trace`, which I didn't touch. With that one lint allowed, clippy is clean on `fox-model` and `fox-engine`.

Everything is in one commit on this branch; nothing is pushed.

probe.fix_hint: 1) Curved edges: `along()` in crates/model/src/regen/extra.rs (around line 532) works on the tessellated polyline from `edge_points()`. It walks the chord lengths and returns a chord direction as the plane normal, and on an arc that chord can be about 1° off the true tangent. It should evaluate the real curve: add a kernel helper in crates/kernel (next to `edge_shape` and `edge_lines` in lib.rs) that uses BRepAdaptor_Curve plus GCPnts_AbscissaPoint to find the parameter at fraction t of the arc length, then returns the point and D1 tangent there, oriented from the edge's start. PointDef::AlongPath uses the same `along()`, so it gets the fix too. 2) Sketch-line paths: `plane` (crates/engine/src/features.rs line 359, via `edge()`/`edge_ref_of` in commands.rs:1788) only takes body edges {point} or {body, edge}. Add a sketch-curve path, e.g. edge: {sketch, curve}, with a model-side variant that resolves the curve in world coordinates (as AxisRef::SketchLine does for axes), and use it in PlaneDef::AlongPath. Fusion measures t from the sketch line's start point.

fix.summary:
Fox's Plane Along Path (`plane method=along_path`) now places the plane the way Fusion does on curved edges, and it accepts a sketch line as the path. All three reference cases (363–365) match Fusion.

**What changed**
- **Kernel:** new `Shape::along_curve(t, from)`. It walks the exact curve (`BRepAdaptor_Curve`, or `BRepAdaptor_CompCurve` for a wire) and uses `GCPnts_AbscissaPoint` to find the point at fraction `t` of the arc length, plus the `D1` tangent there. It measures from whichever end is nearer `from` and points the tangent away from that end. It is exposed through the C++ bridge as `curve_along`.
- **Model:** `along()` (in `regen/extra.rs`) now calls `along_curve` on the edge, measured from the edge's start. It used to take a chord direction from the tessellated polyline, which tilted the plane by about 1° on an arc and made 364 mismatch (volume +1.5%, 8 faces instead of 5). `PointDef::AlongPath` uses the same function, so construction points along a path are exact now too.
- **Sketch paths:** new `PlaneDef::AlongSketch` and `PointDef::AlongSketch { sketch, curve, t }`. They build the sketch curve as a world-space wire and measure `t` from the curve's start point, as Fusion does. Both list the sketch as a dependency.
- **Engine:** the `plane` and `point` `along_path` methods accept `edge: {sketch, curve}` as well as a body edge, with a check that the curve exists. The help text is updated.
- **Script fix:** 365's `part.jsonl` named `"curve": 1` for the sketch line, but the line's id is 2 (points and curves share one id counter, so its end points are 1 and 3). I changed only that id.
- **Tests:** added a kernel unit test that checks the point and tangent on a quarter arc, measured from both ends. Cases 363–365 are added to `baseline.txt`. Only 363 is added to `edit-baseline.txt`, because the test asked only for that one.

**Checks**
- `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes.
- fox-model, fox-kernel and the other fox-engine tests pass, except `fuzz_found_bugs` in `fuzz_features`. It fails at a chamfer step (seed 1022) and fails the same way on the base commit without these changes; it doesn't use along-path.
- `cargo fmt --all` is clean.
- Clippy with `-D warnings` stops in `fox-exchange` and `fox-trace`, which this change doesn't touch. The local clippy is 1.99, newer than CI's pinned 1.97, and its `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint flags existing code there. With only that lint allowed, fox-kernel, fox-model and fox-engine have no warnings.

- **Face references** (`crates/model/src/refs.rs`): `FaceRef::resolve` no longer checks the axis for spheres and matches them by position only.
- **New point reference** (`crates/model/src/construct.rs`, `regen/extra.rs`): `PointRef::SketchCenter {sketch, curve}` gives the world-space centre of a sketch circle, arc, ellipse or elliptical arc. The sketch is recorded as a dependency of the point.

- **385 script** (`part.jsonl`): now calls `{"cmd":"point","method":"center","sketch":3,"curve":2}`. The circle is curve 2 in that sketch, not 1.

The full `-D warnings` run stops on fox-exchange, which this change doesn't touch: the new toolchain's `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint fires there.

1. **Volume.** Fusion's expected volume (9853.77 mm³) is 0.16% under the exact torus volume, 2π²·20·5² = 9869.60 mm³; Fox gets 9869.61. A split can't change the total volume, so Fusion's number is off. Its centre of mass (0.0007, −0.0049, 15.0009) is also off the symmetric (0, 0, 15). This looks like Fusion's low-accuracy physical-properties measurement, and the gap is over the 1e-3 tolerance. Fixing it means re-measuring `expected.json` at higher accuracy, which this task can't edit.
2. **Face count.** OCC's splitter keeps the torus's periodic seam as an edge, so the upper toroidal region comes out as two faces (5 in total, Fusion has 4). `ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain` (OCCT 7.8.1) doesn't merge them, even on a plain `Shape::torus`. It uses `sa.distance_to(&sb)` (closest points of the finite edges) and returns their midpoint. It should take each linear edge as an infinite line (start, end-start) and intersect the two lines: for coplanar lines, solve p1 + s*d1 = p2 + t*d2. Return an error if they're parallel, or if they're skew (the closest points of the infinite lines are more than a small tolerance apart). probe.summary: Fox's tangent plane (`plane` method `tangent` {face, near}) gives the same result as Fusion on cylinders. That holds for Fusion's angle-from-reference-plane option, which Fox reproduces with a `near` point at that angle, both from XZ at 30° and from YZ at −45° on an off-centre cylinder, and for the tangent-at-a-point option. All three cylinder cases match. On a sphere it fails: Fox finds the face when the command runs, but can't find it again when the model rebuilds ("a face could not be found"), and Fusion splits the box fine. Fox also has no direct angle + reference-plane input, only the `near` point.
probe.fix_hint: The bug is in crates/model/src/refs.rs, `FaceRef::resolve`. Its non-planar branch skips any face where `f.normal.dot(n0).abs() < 0.999`. But the C++ `face_infos` in crates/kernel/cpp/kernel.cpp never sets `info.normal` for spheres (it stays [0,0,0]), nor for cones, tori or other surfaces. So a FaceRef to a sphere face never resolves at regen, even though `face_at` (crates/engine/src/commands.rs) picks it fine when the command runs. This breaks `plane` tangent and `axis` normal on spheres, and any other feature that takes a curved non-cylindrical face. There are two possible fixes. One is to skip the alignment test in `resolve` when the stored normal is zero (e.g. `if n0.length_squared() > 0.5 && align.abs() < 0.999 { continue }`), and match on `f.kind` and radius instead. The other is to fill in an axis normal for sphere, cone and torus in kernel.cpp. The first is the safer fix. Optional: `plane` tangent in crates/engine/src/features.rs and `PlaneDef::Tangent` in crates/model/src/regen/extra.rs could also accept Fusion's {angle, reference plane} form. Fusion's convention: at angle 0 the plane is parallel to the reference and touches on the reference's +normal side, and a positive angle rotates it counter-clockwise about the cylinder axis. Fox can already express this with `near`.

fix.summary:
Fox's tangent plane failed on a sphere: the command found the face when it ran, but the model couldn't find it again on rebuild ("a face could not be found"), so the split that used the plane failed too.

Cause: for curved faces, `FaceRef::resolve` (crates/model/src/refs.rs) skipped any face whose axis didn't line up with the stored one. The kernel's `face_infos` leaves the normal at zero for spheres, cones and tori, so a reference to one of those faces could never match.

Fix: a reference with no stored axis now matches only faces that also have no axis, picking the one whose centre is closest to the stored point. References with an axis (cylinders) still need a matching axis, so they work as before. This also fixes any other feature that picks a sphere, cone or torus face, such as `axis` normal.

Cases 391–394 (three cylinder tangent-plane cases and the sphere case) all pass and survive the edit check. I added them to baseline.txt and edit-baseline.txt, and `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` and `cargo test -p fox-model` both pass.

Fox had no equivalent of Fusion's Bounding Solid (Design > SOLID > Create). This adds it as a new parametric feature with a `bounding_solid` command, and case 395-l-plate-box-offset now matches Fusion's measurements.

**Changes**
- **Model**: a new `FeatureKind::BoundingSolid { bodies, shape, plane, offset, sides }`.
  - `bodies` picks which bodies to enclose. It defaults to all of them; it can also be a list of bodies or a component.
  - `shape` is `box` or `cylinder`.
  - `plane` is an optional frame. The default is world XY, and its normal is the cylinder's axis.
  - `offset` grows the solid by the same amount on every side. For a cylinder, that means radially and at both ends.
  - `sides` gives six per-side offsets (-x, +x, -y, +y, -z, +z) that replace `offset`. A cylinder only uses -z and +z.
  - New arms were added at the end of `base_name`, `depends_on` and `for_each_expr`.
  - `crates/model/src/bounding.rs` holds the `BoundShape` enum and the smallest-enclosing-circle code (Welzl's algorithm), with a unit test.
- **Regen** (`crates/model/src/regen/bound.rs`, dispatched from `apply_extra`):

  - A box is that bounding box grown by the offsets.
  - A cylinder uses the smallest circle around the bodies' mesh points, taken across the axis, and spans the bounding box along it.
  - The result is moved back into place and added as a new body; the original bodies stay.
  - Because it rebuilds with the timeline, editing an earlier feature resizes it. That is how the case passes the 15% edit check.

name: Create Form
tooltip:
Enters Form mode and inserts a form feature into the timeline. Use form tools to create and edit history-free bodies by pushing and pulling on vertices, edges, and faces. This is commonly referred to as T-Spline modeling.

Select Finish Form to exit out of the mode.

history.note: Create Form adds a FormFeature to the timeline. In Form mode a T-spline body is built from a control cage, and Finish Form turns it into a smooth B-rep solid. Fusion built both cases from a script: formFeatures.add() → startEdit() → tSplineBodies.addByTSMDescription(TSM) → finishEdit(). I got the TSM by driving Fusion's Form > Box command once through text commands. The smooth 80x60x20 mm cage with 2x2x2 faces gives 75,586.9 mm³ and 6 faces. Pulling the top-centre vertex up gives a dome whose top is at z 28.9 mm. Fox has no T-spline, subdivision or form command at all (only mesh.* and sheet-metal commands), so there is no Fox script; both cases report fox-unbuilt ('no part.jsonl'). Cases: 417-form-box-smooth, 418-form-box-pulled-top.

I got the TSM by driving Fusion's Form > Box command once through text commands. The smooth 80x60x20 mm cage with 2x2x2 faces gives 75,586.9 mm³ and 6 faces. probe.fix_hint: Fox has no Form/T-spline modelling: nothing in crates/ (engine, model, kernel, ui) handles T-splines or subdivision, and the CLI command list has no form.* commands. To support it Fox needs four things. (1) A Form feature in crates/model whose data is a quad control cage: vertices, faces, and crease/smoothness flags per edge. (2) A kernel evaluator in crates/kernel that turns the cage into a B-rep. The simplest route is Catmull-Clark limit surfaces, with regular quads as bicubic B-spline patches; you can also go the other way and fit each patch to a Geom_BSplineSurface and sew them. Cage faces map to B-rep faces: the 2x2x2 box gives 6 faces in Fusion, so the patches on each side are merged. (3) Engine commands: at least form.box (plane, length/width/height, face counts) and form.move_vertex. A form.from_cage command taking raw vertices and faces would let the test cases be written straight from the TSM 'g' lines. (4) A part.jsonl for these two cases once the commands exist. The expected.json files hold Fusion's numbers. Fusion's corners are G1CAPS with star-knot-rule NURCCS, so a plain Catmull-Clark limit may differ slightly in volume near the cage corners.

fix.summary:
Fox had no form, T-spline or subdivision modelling, so it couldn't build reference cases 417-form-box-smooth and 418-form-box-pulled-top. Both now build and match Fusion's numbers.

**Model** (`crates/model/src/form.rs`, `regen/form.rs`)
- New `FeatureKind::Form { plane, cage, operation }`. The cage is a closed quad mesh in the plane's coordinates.
- The body is the cage's Catmull-Clark limit surface. Cage faces are subdivided as grids, and vertices are pushed to their exact limit positions.
- The surface is split into B-rep faces along "star lines": edge lines that leave each extraordinary vertex (valence other than 4) and run straight through regular vertices.
  - Each region they bound that is a rectangular grid of cage faces becomes one bicubic B-spline face, interpolated through limit points with not-a-knot ends.
  - Any other region gets one face per cage face.
  - A box cage therefore gives one face per side, as in Fusion (6 faces).
- The faces are sewn into a solid.
- Cages that aren't closed, are wound inconsistently, or are pinched at a vertex are rejected with an error.

**Kernel** (`cpp/form.cpp`, `src/form.rs`)
- New `Shape::bspline_face(&BSplineSurface)` builds a face from poles and knots, using the usual try/catch so a failure becomes an error rather than a crash.

**Engine** (`crates/engine/src/form.rs`)
- `form.box`: Fusion's Form > Box, with length, width, height and faces per side (default 2), plus optional `at` and `operation`.
- `form.cage`: takes raw vertices and quad faces.
- `form.move_vertex`: pulls a cage vertex, picked by index or nearest point, to a position (`to`) or by an offset (`by`).

**UI**
- The "Create Form" placeholders under Solid > Create and Surface > Create now open a box form dialog.

**Results**
- Volume and area are within 0.065% of Fusion (tolerance is 0.1%). For 417: 75,538.2 vs 75,586.9 mm³.
- Bounding boxes match, including the 418 dome top at z 28.889, and the face count is 6.
- The remaining gap comes from Fusion's G1 star-point caps, which differ slightly from the plain Catmull-Clark limit near the cage corners.

**Tests**
- New: engine `tests_form.rs` and model unit tests in `form.rs`.
- Both cases are added to `baseline.txt`; `reference_parts` passes.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes.
- Clippy (`-D warnings`) is clean on kernel, model, engine and ui with one lint allowed. The local toolchain is Rust 1.99, newer than CI's pinned 1.97, and its new `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint fires in fox-exchange and fox-trace, which this change doesn't touch.
- `fuzz_features::fuzz_found_bugs` fails (seed 1022 chamfer), but it fails identically on the base commit's sources, so this change didn't cause it.
