probe.summary: Fusion's Pattern on Path copies features or bodies along a sketch path. The options that change geometry are the quantity, the distance (spacing between copies, or an extent the copies are spread over), the start point (0 to 1 along the path), flip, symmetric, and orientation (identical, or turned to follow the path). Fusion built all four cases cleanly and wrote expected.json for each. Fox has no path-pattern command: every Fox script stops at `pattern.path` with "unknown command", and the existing reference case 53-path-pattern only fakes it with moved sketch copies. The candidate commands Fox suggested (sheet.flat_pattern, sketch.pattern_rect/circ, pattern.rectangular) are unrelated.
probe.fix_hint: Add a `pattern.path` command in crates/engine, next to pattern.rectangular and pattern.circular. Its parameters would be: path (a sketch id); path_curves (optional, chained in order); count; then either spacing, or distance with extent:true; start (0 to 1, where distance is measured from; default 0); flip; symmetric; orientation: identical | along_path; bodies or features; join. Copy k sits at arc length s_k = start*L ± k*spacing; for extent, spacing = distance/(count-1). Copies are translated by path(s_k) − path(s_0). With along_path, each copy is also rotated by the change in tangent angle at path(s_k) relative to path(s_0). Symmetric adds copies at −k*spacing; past the ends of a line path Fusion extends the line straight (the symmetric case puts copies at x −30 on a path starting at x 0). Flip runs toward the path start, so start=1 with flip walks back along the chain and around its corner. Feature patterns (re-running a cut at each copy, as in hole-extent-arc) also need a feature-pattern path like the replay that 10-rect-pattern-holes and 53-path-pattern emulate. Each probe's part.jsonl already calls the proposed `pattern.path`, so it can serve as the test once the command exists. I also changed tools/fusion-bridge/FoxBridge/recipe_runner.py: a new op_path_pattern (pattern_of, features/bodies, path {sketch, curves}, count, spacing or distance + distance_type extent, start_point, flip, symmetric, orientation). It switches the design's display units to mm first, because Fusion stores the pattern distance in display units rounded to their precision: in inches, 15 mm became 0.591 in, which is 15.011 mm. Fusion quirk: startPoint=0.5 on a line gave odd offsets (−35 and −70 mm instead of +15 and +30), so no case uses a start point inside the path.

fix.summary:
Adds a `pattern.path` command, which works like Fusion's Pattern on Path. It copies bodies, or re-applies the tool solids of features, at points spaced by arc length along a sketch path made of chained curves.

Options: count; spacing, or a distance with `extent: true` (the copies are spread over that length); start (a fraction from 0 to 1 along the path); flip (run toward the path's start); symmetric (copies on both sides of the original, `count` in total); orientation (`identical`, or `along_path`, which turns each copy by the change in the path's tangent); bodies or features; join. As in Fusion, copies past the path's ends sit on the path's straight extensions, and a flipped pattern that starts at the end walks back around the chain's corners.

Fox has no section type and no partial-path distance, and it silently ignores those keys, so it builds a round full-length pipe instead. The square-section case comes out 21% too small with 5 faces instead of 10. The triangular case cut at distance one 0.6 comes out 127% too big, with the wrong bounding box and 5 faces instead of 7. probe.summary: I tested Fusion's Pipe along a line, tangent R20 arc, line path on the XZ plane. Fox's `pipe` matches Fusion exactly for a solid round pipe (d=6) and a hollow one (1 mm wall). Fox has no section type and no partial-path distance, and it silently ignores those keys, so it builds a round full-length pipe instead. The square-section case comes out 21% too small with 5 faces instead of 10. The triangular case cut at distance one 0.6 comes out 127% too big, with the wrong bounding box and 5 faces instead of 7.
probe.fix_hint: In Fox, `pipe` (crates/engine/src/features.rs, the "pipe" arm, plus FeatureKind::Pipe in crates/model/src/lib.rs) only takes diameter and wall. Its regen in crates/model/src/regen/extra.rs always sweeps a circle of radius diameter/2. The fix needs to add three things. (1) A `section` parameter: circular, square or triangular. The size is the diameter, the square's side, or the equilateral triangle's side. Square: a centred 6x6 square at size 6 gives Fusion's numbers exactly (volume 36 x path length). Triangle: in Fusion's triangle the vertex is 2√3 from the path on the -X side at the start, and the centroid sits 1 mm off the path toward -Y (world). Use the triangular-partial-path expected.json to work out the exact placement. The hollow wall applies to every section as an inward offset. (2) `distance_one` and `distance_two` (fractions 0..1 of the path length from each end) to trim the path before sweeping. (3) Reject unknown keys, or at least `section` and `distance`, instead of silently building a round full-length pipe. In the Fox scripts I used the keys "section" and "distance". To test this in Fusion I added op_pipe to tools/fusion-bridge/FoxBridge/recipe_runner.py; its recipe keys are section, size, wall, distance_one and distance_two.

fix.summary:
Fox's `pipe` could only sweep a circle along the whole path. It also silently ignored `section` and `distance`, so square and partial pipes came out as round full-length ones. The 4 Fusion cases (84 to 87) now match expected.json and are added to baseline.txt.

**Changes**
- **Model:** `FeatureKind::Pipe` has two new fields, both serde-defaulted so older .fox files still load:
  - `section`: a new `PipeSection` enum with circular, square and triangular.
  - `distance`: the fraction of the path to follow, measured from its start. `for_each_expr` visits it.
- **Section shapes** (in `regen/extra.rs`):
  - The section plane's x runs across the path in the sketch plane and its y along the sketch normal.
  - Square: a centred square whose side is the size.
  - Triangular: an equilateral triangle whose *height* is the size, so its side is 2/√3 × size. The base is centred on the path at −size/2 along the sketch normal and the apex is at +size/2, so the centroid sits size/6 below the path. I worked this out from the answer key: the area is 12√3 for size 6, the Y range is ±3, the centroid y is −1 and the X range is ±2√3.
  - The wall is an inward offset for every section shape.
  - Square and triangular pipes are run through `unified()` so each flat side is one face along its straight runs, as in Fusion (10 and 7 faces).
- **Partial path:** before sweeping, the path is cut to its first `distance` × length. This is exact for lines and arcs. Splines and ellipse arcs are measured by sampling; spline pieces are split at the cut (de Casteljau) and ellipse arcs shortened.
- **Command:** `pipe` takes `section` (circular, square or triangular), `size` as another name for `diameter`, and `distance` or `distance_one`. It now rejects keys it doesn't know and unknown section names. The help text is updated.
- **UI:** the Pipe form has new Section and Distance inputs.
- **Tests and docs:** a new engine test, `pipe_sections_and_partial_paths`, checks volumes, the triangle's placement, half of a spline path, and the rejection of unknown keys. The README line on pipes is updated.

**Checks**
- `reference_parts` passes, all four new cases included.
- The fox-model, fox-engine and fox-ui tests pass, except `fuzz_found_bugs` in `crates/engine/tests/fuzz_features.rs`. It fails on seed 1022 with "Body1 is not a valid solid" after chamfer and cut steps. That test never calls pipe and nothing it runs uses the changed code, but I didn't run it on main to confirm it was failing before.
- `cargo fmt` is clean.
- Clippy is clean on fox-model, fox-engine and fox-ui only after allowing one new lint (`chunks_exact_to_as_chunks`). The local toolchain is Rust 1.99, while CI pins 1.97 (which isn't installed here), and that lint fires on existing fox-exchange code.

**Limits**
- `distance_two` isn't supported: the command rejects it rather than guessing what it means.
- The triangle's apex direction (toward the sketch normal) comes from this one Fusion case only.

Fox's `pattern.rectangular` could only pattern one way and had no extent distance type, so case 443 (symmetric) didn't match Fusion and case 444 had to fake its extent with spacing "30 mm / 3". All four cases now match Fusion.

**What changed**
- **Model** (`crates/model/src/lib.rs`): `FeatureKind::RectangularPattern` has three new options: `symmetric`, `symmetric2` and `extent`. All default to false and are skipped when saving if false, so older designs load and save the same as before.
- **Regen** (`crates/model/src/regen.rs`): a new `pattern_offsets` helper places the instances. The original is skipped by its index, not by having a zero offset, so a pattern with 0 spacing still makes its copies as it did before.
- **Command** (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`): `pattern.rectangular` now reads `symmetric`, `symmetric2` and `distance_type` (`spacing` or `extent`). These match the options `sketch.pattern_rect` already had, and the help text is updated.

- **Fusion recipe runner** (`tools/fusion-bridge/FoxBridge/recipe_runner.py`): it now applies a recipe's per-direction `symmetric` and its extent distance type. With no second direction it sets quantityTwo to 1, because Fusion otherwise keeps its default count there and adds extra copies.

**How Fusion places instances** (checked by running Fusion 2705 through the bridge, including the even counts the probe didn't test)
- A symmetric direction with count n puts the original at index (n−1)/2, rounded down, and the extra instance of an even count goes on the positive side:
  - 3 at 12 mm gives −12, 0, +12
  - 4 gives −12, 0, 12, 24
  - 2 gives 0, 12 (not centred)
- With extent, the distance runs from the original to the farthest instance on the positive side. Symmetric with 4 instances over 12 mm gives a 6 mm step, at −6, 0, 6, 12.
- A new unit test, `rectangular_pattern_symmetric_and_extent_offsets`, checks these values.

Fusion built all four and Fox mismatches on every one. Fusion resizes the cylinder to the size and class mean diameter, even for a cosmetic thread (the M8 6g rod becomes Ø7.866). It also cuts a truncated ISO profile and makes few faces (6 on the rod, 7 in the tube). Fox keeps the drawn diameter and cuts a sharp 60° V groove, giving 20 and 18 faces. The volume differences run from -3.9% to +9.1%, and Fox puts the partial-length thread at the other end of the rod. probe.summary: I tested Fusion's Thread against Fox's `thread` command with four cases: a modeled external M10 thread on a rod, a modeled internal M10 thread in a tube bore, a partial left-hand M12 thread with a length and offset, and a cosmetic M8 thread. Fusion built all four and Fox mismatches on every one. Fusion resizes the cylinder to the size and class mean diameter, even for a cosmetic thread (the M8 6g rod becomes Ø7.866). It also cuts a truncated ISO profile and makes few faces (6 on the rod, 7 in the tube). Fox keeps the drawn diameter and cuts a sharp 60° V groove, giving 20 and 18 faces. The volume differences run from -3.9% to +9.1%, and Fox puts the partial-length thread at the other end of the rod.
probe.fix_hint:
The gap is in the `FeatureKind::Thread` arm of crates/model/src/regen/extra.rs and in `thread_groove` in the same file. Four changes would close it:

1. **Diameter:** Fox only knows the pitch. It needs thread size and class data, as Fusion's `ThreadInfo` has (the designation, the class and the major, minor and pitch diameters). It should then resize the selected cylinder before threading, for both cosmetic and modeled threads. External threads go to the class-mean major diameter (M10 6g → Ø9.85, M12 6g → Ø11.8335, M8 6g → Ø7.866). Internal threads go to the class-mean minor diameter. Today a cosmetic thread leaves the solid untouched.
2. **Profile:** cut the ISO 68-1 truncated profile between those diameters, with a P/8 flat at the crest and a P/4 flat at the root. Fox now cuts a sharp 60° V with a fixed depth (0.6134P external, 0.5413P internal) measured from the drawn radius.
3. **Start end:** with `length` and `offset` and no flip, Fox measures from the opposite end to Fusion's default low end on a +Z-extruded rod. The centre-of-mass z is 14.79 in Fox and 15.29 in Fusion. The end that `cylinder_extent`'s t0 maps to should match Fusion's LowEnd (the z=0 end here).
4. **Faces:** Fox's `helix_sweep` groove splits into many faces (20 against 6 on the rod, 18 against 7 in the tube). Fusion builds the thread as a single helical face set.

I also added an `op_thread` to tools/fusion-bridge/FoxBridge/recipe_runner.py. It takes `face` or `faces`, `internal`, `thread_type`, `designation`, `class`, `modeled`, `right_handed`, `full_length`, `length`, `offset` and `location` (`low_end` or `high_end`).

fix.summary:
Fox's `thread` command now builds threads the way Fusion's Thread command does. All four new reference cases (92–95) pass and survive the 15% edit check. They are added to `baseline.txt` and `edit-baseline.txt`. `cargo test -p fox-engine --test reference_parts` passes with no regressions.

**What changed**
- **Size and class (diameter):**
  - `thread` now takes an ISO metric `designation` (`M10x1.5`, or `M10` for the coarse pitch) and a `class` (default `6g` outside, `6H` inside). It also accepts Fusion-style `location: low_end|high_end` and `right_handed`.
  - The selected cylinder is resized to the class-mean diameter for cosmetic and modeled threads alike: the major diameter outside, the minor diameter inside. For example, M8 6g gives Ø7.866 and M10 6H gives a Ø8.526 bore.
  - The diameters come from the ISO 965-1 deviation and tolerance tables in a new `fox_model::thread` module.
  - Without a designation, the drawn diameter is taken as the basic size and the solid is not resized, so older designs keep their size.
- **Profile:** a modeled thread cuts the ISO 68-1 profile: 60° flanks half a pitch apart at the class-mean pitch diameter, with a flat root.
  - I fitted the root diameter from Fusion's measured volume and area: outside, the mean of d1 max and d3 min; inside, the mean of D and D2 max + 11H/12.
  - The same fit reproduced the class-mean pitch diameters (8.928 and 9.116) to within about 0.0002.
- **Thread ends:** the groove is swept a pitch past each end, then cut off by planes square to the axis at the thread's ends. Fusion's partial-thread area and face count only match this.
- **Start end:** `length` and `offset` now count from the face's low end along a fixed axis direction, matching Fusion's LowEnd.
- **Face count:** a helical cut leaves the crest cylinder as one strip per turn.
  - A new kernel step, `merge_cylinder_strips` (`cpp/threads.cpp`), joins the strips into one face. This gives Fusion's counts: 6 faces on the rod, 7 in the tube, 8 on the partial thread.
  - OCCT's standard integration is inaccurate on a face that wraps more than one turn. For such shapes, `mass_props` now measures volume against a plane square to the axis, where the crest contributes nothing. Other shapes are measured exactly as before.
- **Bore picking bug:** `FaceRef::resolve` now also scores curved faces by distance to the surface. A tube's bore and outer wall share a centroid, so picking the bore used to resolve to the outer cylinder.
- **Scripts:** the four `part.jsonl` scripts now pass the recipe's designation and class instead of only a pitch.
- **Tests:** the thread form gained size and class fields. New tests cover the ISO class means, the strip merge in the kernel, and engine threads by size and class.

**Test status**
- `cargo fmt` is clean.
- Clippy is clean on the changed crates. The local toolchain (1.99, newer than CI's pinned 1.97) flags a new `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint, but only in crates this PR doesn't touch.
- `fuzz_found_bugs` (seed 1022, no threads involved) fails, and fails the same way on unmodified HEAD.
fix.title: Model threads by ISO size and class, as Fusion's Thread does

history.note: I tested Fusion's Sketch.importSVG(file, x, y, scale) against Fox's sketch.insert from an SVG file on three SVGs. In both apps the curves come out the same shape (volume and area match in the px cases), but Fusion always reads SVG units as 96-dpi px, ignoring a mm width/height with a viewBox, and puts the SVG's (0,0) on the sketch origin with y negated. Fox honours the mm size and mirrors y about the middle of the viewBox, so every case lands 26.46 mm higher in y, and the mm case is also 3.78x larger. Cases: 472-mm-viewbox-plate-hole, 473-px-path-arc-offset-scale, 474-group-transform-cubic.

It changes mass and the BOM, but not volume, area, bounding box or face count, and the probe only compares those, so building geometry can't test it. Fox has a matching command, component.material, which sets a component's material for mass and the BOM. A UI probe or a mass-comparison probe could check material densities and the resulting masses.
probe.fix_hint: There's no geometry gap. A later mass probe should check two things. First, whether Fox's material library densities (Steel, Aluminum 6061, ABS and so on) match Fusion's. Second, whether component.material changes mass the same way in inspect.center_of_mass and assembly.bom. Fusion can also assign a material to a single body (BRepBody.material), while Fox's command takes only a component. In a quick test, passing "root" as the component was rejected ("missing or invalid 'component'"), so the root component may not be addressable by name.

tooltip:
Forms uneven T-Spline geometry into a smooth cylindrical shape.

Select a face on the feature to cylindrify. The preview displays automatically. Uncheck Auto Feature Selection to select individual faces.

name: Edit By Curve
tooltip:
Manipulates T-Spline edges using a driving curve.

Select edges to create a driving curve. Move the control points to adjust the shape of the T-Spline edges.

name: Edit Form
tooltip:
Manipulates faces, edges and vertices with transform, scale and rotate editing.

Select faces, edges, or vertices to enable the manipulator. Double click a face or edge to select a loop.

name: Erase And Fill
tooltip:
Deletes a part of connected T-Spline geometry and fills new gaps with faces. You can use this to remove struts or bridges.

Select the faces to erase and select fill type.

name: Fill Hole
tooltip:
Fills an internal hole in T-Spline body.

Select the edge of the hole and set the fill type.

name: Flatten
tooltip:
Projects vertices to a best fit or user defined plane.

Select the vertices and/or tangency handles to flatten.

name: Freeze
tooltip:
Freezes faces and edges on the model to prevent accidental changes.

Select faces or edges to freeze.

name: Insert Edge
tooltip:
Inserts edges at a specified position from the original edge.

Select an edge or double click to select a loop.

name: Insert Point
tooltip:
Inserts an edge by selecting two points.

Select a point on an edge to start. Continue selecting points on additional edges to divide multiple faces.

name: Interpolate
tooltip:
Switches the location of the surface and the control points to improve fitting. Select whether to move the control points to the surface or the surface to the control points.

Select the body then set whether you are moving control points or surface points.

name: Match
tooltip:
Aligns the edges of a T-Spline body with sketch curves or edges on a solid or surface body.

Select the T-Spline edges, then select the sketch curves or edges on a solid or surface body to match.

name: Merge Edge
tooltip:
Aligns the first set of selected edges to a second set of selected edges.

Select the first set of edges then the second set of edges.

name: Pull
tooltip:
Snaps selected T-Spline vertices to a face or surface. The vertices could be control points or surface points.

Select the vertices to move and the vertices will automatically move to the nearest body.

name: Slide Edge
tooltip:
Moves the selected edge along the control polygon.

Select the edges then specify the new position.

name: Smooth
tooltip:
Smoothes an area of the T-Spline geometry.

Select the faces to smooth and the smoothing rate.

name: Straighten
tooltip:
Straightens vertices to a best fit line, an existing line, or a line through two selected points.

Select the direction type, select a line or two points to define the line, then select the vertices or tangency handles to straighten.

name: Subdivide
tooltip:
Divides one or more faces into a subset of faces.

Select T-Spline faces to divide, then select the Insert Mode and adjust the number of faces to divide selected faces into. Optionally for Simple Mode, check Object Snap and specify the Offset distance.

name: Thicken
tooltip:
Creates a body offset.

Select the body then set the thickness and end treatments.

name: UnCrease
tooltip:
Restores previously creased edges to their original state.

Select creased edges to uncrease.

name: UnFreeze
tooltip:
Unfreezes faces and edges that have previously been frozen.

Select faces or edges to unfreeze.

name: UnWeld Edges
tooltip:
Disconnects an edge or loop.

Select an edge or double click to select a loop. Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (Mac) to select multiple edges.

name: Weld Vertices
tooltip:
Joins two or more vertices.

Select two vertices to join. Window select vertices to weld within the specified tolerance.

name: Circular - Duplicate
tooltip:
Create specified number of duplicate bodies around a selected axis.

Select the body to copy then select the axis to revolve around.

name: Circular - Internal
tooltip:
Creates circular symmetry with the elements of a T-Spline body.

Select a face on the body then select the number of symmetry lines.

name: Clear Symmetry
tooltip:
Remove symmetry constraint from individual bodies or a series of bodies.

Select the symmetric bodies.

name: Isolate Symmetry
tooltip:
Prevents symmetric transformations from being applied to the selected vertex, edge or face.

Select the faces, edges, or vertices to remove symmetry from.

name: Mirror - Duplicate
tooltip:
Create a duplicate body mirrored across a specified plane.

Select the body to copy then select the mirror plane.

name: Mirror - Internal
tooltip:
Creates a mirror symmetry with the elements of a T-Spline body.

Select a face on each side of the body. If needed select edges on each side, then vertices.

name: Display Mode
tooltip:
Sets the body display to smooth, box, or control frame. Smooth shows the actual model. Box displays only the control framework. Control frame displays the framework and the actual model.

Select the desired display mode. If there is more than one T-Spline body, you need to select the body to change the display.

name: Enable Better Performance
tooltip: Toggles between better performance or better display. Better display shows the bodies at highest quality (G1 conditions at star points). Better performance calculates modification by applying G0 conditions at star points.

name: Make Uniform
tooltip:
Evenly distributes the angles at the intersection of star points and makes faces as uniform as possible.

Select a T-Spline body to make uniform.

name: Repair Body
tooltip:
Analyzes the T-Spline body and displays information about the mesh. Corrects Error T and Error Star conditions.

Select the body to analyze.

name: Create Base Mesh Feature
tooltip: Creates an empty Mesh Base Feature.

name: Create Mesh Section Sketch
tooltip:
Creates a sketch that contains a section line where a plane intersects a mesh body.

Select a mesh body, select a plane, then adjust the location of the section line. Edit the sketch and use the Fit Curves To Mesh Section command to create sketch geometry to match the section line.

name: Tessellate
tooltip:
Converts an existing solid or surface body into a mesh body.

Select the solid or surface body to tessellate, then adjust the mesh refinement settings to convert the body to a mesh body.

name: Attract to Reference
tooltip:
Attracts selected faces on a mesh body towards a reference mesh body.

Select faces on a mesh body to edit, select a reference mesh body, then adjust density, smoothness, and offset to control the attraction.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Bridge
tooltip:
Bridges two regions of a mesh body by creating connecting geometry between them.

Select two face groups or sets of faces on a mesh body, then adjust the density to bridge them together.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Close Cracks
tooltip:
Closes small cracks and gaps in a mesh body.

Select a mesh body to close cracks and seal small gaps between triangles.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Combine
tooltip:
Joins, intersects, cuts, or merges two or more mesh bodies to create a single mesh body.

Select the target body, select one or more tool bodies to combine with the target body, then select the operation to use to combine the bodies together.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Convert Mesh
tooltip:
Converts a mesh body to a solid or surface body.

Select the mesh body to convert, then select the operation and method. In the browser and the canvas, the mesh body converts to a solid or surface body. Face groups are used to infer prismatic features.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Convert To Quad Mesh
tooltip:
Converts a mesh body or face groups with triangular faces to a mesh body or face groups with quad faces.

Select a mesh body or face groups, select an output type, then adjust the settings to convert from triangular to quad faces.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Direct Edit
tooltip:
Creates a mesh base feature that you can edit directly.

Select the mesh body to edit. A mesh base feature displays on the timeline and you can make local modifications to the mesh body without capturing the changes in the parametric history of the design.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Erase And Fill
tooltip:
Removes and replaces faces on a mesh body to fill holes and repair regions.

Select the boundary of faces around a hole to fill, or select the faces of a region to remove and replace.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Mesh Align
tooltip:
Aligns a face on a mesh body to a plane with one transformation.

Select a mesh face, then select a plane to align the body to.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Plane Cut
tooltip:
Uses a plane to trim or split a mesh body.

Select a mesh body, then select and position the cutting plane. The cut can trim the body, split the body into multiple bodies, or split the faces only. For the Trim and Split Body cut types, select a fill type to generate watertight bodies.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Reduce
tooltip:
Reduces the number of faces on a mesh body to minimize complexity.

Select a mesh body or face groups, select a reduction target, then adjust the settings to reduce the number of mesh faces.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Remesh
tooltip:
Refines or coarsens faces on a mesh body or face groups.

Select a mesh body or face groups on a mesh body, then adjust the settings to regenerate the mesh faces.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Remove
tooltip:
Remove meshes

Select the mesh bodies to be removed. For every mesh which is removed, a feature appears in the timeline. The removal can be, in contrast to delete, be undone and meshes can be restored parametrically.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Reverse Normal
tooltip:
Reverses the normal direction of selected faces on a mesh body.

Select faces on a mesh body to reverse their normal direction.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Scale Mesh
tooltip:
Scales mesh bodies from a reference point.

Select mesh bodies, select a reference point to scale from and a scale type, then specify the scale factor to scale the mesh bodies.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Separate
tooltip:
Separates regions of a mesh body into independent mesh bodies.

Select a separation type, then select a mesh body or face groups to separate into individual bodies.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Shell
tooltip:
Hollows the interior of a mesh body.

Select a mesh body, then adjust the direction and thickness to hollow the interior volume.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Smooth
tooltip:
Smooths rough or creased regions on a mesh body.

Select a mesh body or face groups, select a smoothing type, then adjust the smoothness and scale to smooth rough or creased regions.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Smooth Boundary
tooltip:
Smooths the boundary edges of a mesh body.

Select a mesh body or face groups to smooth the boundary edges, improving mesh quality near open boundaries.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Texture Extrude
tooltip:
Uses an image to add surface texture to a mesh body.

Select faces, face groups, or a mesh body to add texture to and choose an image to use for the texture. Specify the extrude type and distance then adjust the image scale and placement.

Optionally, repeat the texture in a grid pattern across the selected geometry.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Modify

name: Combine Face Groups
tooltip:
Combines two or more adjacent face groups on a mesh body.

To display face groups, toggle Inspect > Display Mesh Face Groups. Select two or more adjacent face groups on the mesh body to combine them.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Prepare

name: Create Face Group
tooltip:
Creates a face group from a selection of faces on a mesh body.

To display face groups, toggle Inspect > Display Mesh Face Groups. Select faces on a mesh body to include in the face group. Adjust the settings in the Mesh Selection Palette to refine the selection set.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Prepare

name: Generate Face Groups
tooltip:
Automatically generates face groups on a mesh body using the normal angles between faces to determine the boundaries of each face group.

To display face groups, toggle Inspect > Display Mesh Face Groups. Select mesh bodies or face groups, select the generation method, then adjust the face opening angle, tolerance, and minimal area ratio.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Prepare

name: Repair
tooltip:
Repairs a mesh body to prepare it for further design and manufacturing operations.

Select a mesh body to repair, then select a repair type. For the Rebuild repair type, select a rebuild type, then adjust density and offset.
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Prepare

name: Mesh Palette
paths: Sheet Metal > Direct Mesh Editing > Select

name: Boss
tooltip:
Creates a boss feature to fasten two solid bodies together and reinforce thin areas of a design.

Select a sketch point between two solid bodies, then adjust the settings for each side of the boss feature and the fastener that will assemble them together.

name: Lip
tooltip:
Creates a lip, groove, or combined feature on one or two solid bodies.

Select an edge on a solid body then choose between the Lip, Groove, or Lip And Groove types. Select a guide type, a pull direction or guide face to locate the feature, then adjust the dimension settings. Optionally, select one or two extents for the feature and choose a result option.

name: Rest
tooltip:
Creates a rest feature that intersects the overall shape and forms a flat area that can be used for other features or placement of other components.

Select a closed sketch profile and a solid body, then specify the thickness.

name: Snap Fit
tooltip:
Creates a cantilever snap fit feature to fasten two solid bodies together in a design.

Select a snap fit type, select a sketch point between two solid bodies, then adjust the settings for the hook, groove, or loop on each side of the snap fit feature.

name: Design Advice
tooltip:
Identifies manufacturability concerns based on best practices for plastic injection molding, and provides recommendations to address them.

Select a solid body and the pull direction, then click Analyze. Once the analysis is complete, the rules, results, and recommendations display.

name: Assign Plastic Rule
tooltip:
Assigns a plastic rule to a component to automatically control the properties of plastic features, like physical material and thickness.

Select a component, then select the plastic rule to assign to it.

name: Manage Plastic Rules
tooltip:
Manages plastic rules in the active design to automatically control properties of plastic features, like physical material and thickness.

Create new rules, edit existing rules, or save rules to a library to use them in multiple designs.

name: Create PCB Sketch
tooltip:
Unavailable when board is not defined.

To use 3D PCB tools, first edit the outline sketch to draw a closed profile, then Define Board to select a profile to create the PCB body.

name: Define Board
tooltip:
Defines the PCB board outline and 2D coordinate system.

Select one or more closed profiles from the Board Outline Sketch or mechanical assembly. Choose a point for the origin of the 2D coordinate system and an edge for the X axis. Flip the X and Z axes to set the desired Y axis.

name: Edit Board Outline Sketch
tooltip:
Edits the primary sketch that defines the board outline.

Create a closed profile to define the board. You can project geometry from the assembly context to ensure the PCB outline stays updated with the mechanical assembly.

name: PCBHole
tooltip:
Unavailable when board is not defined.

To use 3D PCB tools, first edit the outline sketch to draw a closed profile, then Define Board to select a profile to create the PCB body.

name: Flip Component
tooltip:
Unavailable when board is not defined.

To use 3D PCB tools, first edit the outline sketch to draw a closed profile, then Define Board to select a profile to create the PCB body.

name: Move Component
tooltip:
Unavailable when board is not defined.

To use 3D PCB tools, first edit the outline sketch to draw a closed profile, then Define Board to select a profile to create the PCB body.

name: 3D PCB Settings
tooltip:
Provides presets to help configure which objects display in the 3D PCB document and whether or not bitmap images are used to represent traces.

Select the 2D PCB objects you want represented in the 3D PCB document. Components without a 3D model are identified so you can decide whether or not to exclude them. Included components without 3D models are represented by rectangular shapes.

name: Link to 2D PCB
tooltip:
Unavailable when board is not defined.

To use 3D PCB tools, first edit the outline sketch to draw a closed profile, then Define Board to select a profile to create the PCB body.

name: Push to 2D PCB
tooltip:
Unavailable when board is not defined.

To use 3D PCB tools, first edit the outline sketch to draw a closed profile, then Define Board to select a profile to create the PCB body.

name: 2D PCB
tooltip: Switches to a 2D layout of the physical printed circuit board that defines component placement and routing. If no 2D PCB exists, creates 2D PCB.

name: Schematic
tooltip:
Unavailable when there is no linked schematic. To link a schematic, create or open an electronics design.
Switches to a logical representation of the electronic circuit that defines signals and connections.

name: Publish Video
tooltip: Publish animation to video file format.

name: New Storyboard
tooltip: Create an additional Storyboard tab, which creates a new timeline.

name: Appearance
tooltip:
The appearance affects the color of bodies, components, and faces. Appearances override the color assigned from the physical material. Appearances do not affect engineering properties.

Drag the appearance from the dialog to the body, component, or face.

name: Auto Explode: All Levels
tooltip: Explode all levels of the assembly, down to the lowest leaf parts for a complete exploded view.

name: Auto Explode: One Level
tooltip: Explode the first level children components of the assembly.

name: Manual Explode
tooltip: Manually select components and define the axis they should explode along.

name: Restore Home
tooltip: Automatically moves the component back to its original home location, as defined in the Design Workspace.

name: Show/Hide
tooltip: Turn on or off the visibility of components in the scene instantly or fade over a duration of time.

name: Transform Components
tooltip: Select the components to move then specify the distance and/or angle to move them in space. These movements will be captured on the timeline to create an animation of the movement.

name: View
tooltip: Toggle Camera Recording on or off. Toggling the view off allows non-recorded scene navigation.

name: Automation Preferences
tooltip:
Lets you set automation for this drawing template. Control view placement, dimensions, and sheet creation.

Templates with placed views have only Auto Dimension preferences.

name: Coincident
tooltip:
Constrains the position of two points or a point and a line or a curve together

This could be a point constrained along a line, two points constrained to each other, or a point constrained along a curve.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Collinear
tooltip:
Constrains two or more objects so that they share a common line.

This could be a line and a rectangle, where the line and one edge of the rectangle lie along the same line.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Concentric
tooltip: Constrains two or more arcs, circles, or ellipses to the same center point.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Equal
tooltip: Constrains similar objects so that their sizes are identical. When the size of one object changes, the others adjust, too.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Fix
tooltip: Locks the size and location of a point or an object.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Horizontal/Vertical
tooltip: Constrains a single line on either a vertical or horizontal axis, whichever is closer to the current alignment.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Parallel
tooltip: Constrains two lines so that they extend in the same direction and never intersect.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Perpendicular
tooltip: Constrains two objects so that they lie perpendicular (at a 90-degree angle) to each other.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Symmetric
tooltip: Constrains two or more objects so that they are symmetrical (identical to each other in relation to a common axis).
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Tangent
tooltip: Constrains a curve and another object so that they touch at a single point but never cross each other.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Constraints
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Constraints

name: Auxiliary View
tooltip:
Creates a projected view that is aligned to an edge in a parent view.

Select an edge in a parent view, place the projected view, then adjust the view's style, scale and edge visibility.

name: Base View
tooltip:
Creates a view of the referenced design.

Place the view, then adjust the view's orientation, style, scale, and edge visibility. Once created, projected, section and detail views are derived from this view.

name: Base View Placeholder
tooltip:
Generates a base view placeholder.

When the drawing template is used to create a new drawing, the placeholder is updated to show the referenced design.

name: Break View
tooltip:
Shortens an existing view by removing a portion of the design.

Select a parent view, select horizontal or vertical, specify the start of the break, then specify the end of the break. The portion of the design between the breaks is removed.

name: Breakout Section View
tooltip:
Removes a defined area of material to expose inner features in an existing drawing view.

Select a parent view, then specify the shape and depth of the area of material to remove.

name: Create Sketch
tooltip:
Create Sketch

Create a new sketch on the current sheet.

Click a view for a linked sketch, or click
outside the view for an independent sketch

Use Finish Sketch to exit.

name: Crop View
tooltip:
Removes an unwanted portion of the view image.

Select a view and drag the crop window.

name: Detail View
tooltip:
Creates a circular detail view of a portion of the design.

Select a parent view, specify the center point of the detail boundary, specify the size of the detail boundary, then place the detail view. The detail view's scale is increased to the next scale.

name: Perspective View
tooltip:
Displays designs in three-point perspective.

Parallel lines converge on a vanishing point which provides a sense of how the human eye, or a camera, perceives real objects.

name: Projected View
tooltip:
Creates projected orthogonal and isometric views of the design.

Select a parent view, then place projected views as required.

name: Projected View Placeholder
tooltip:
Generates projected and isometric view placeholders.

When the drawing template is used to create a new drawing, the placeholders are updated to show the referenced design.

name: Section View
tooltip:
Creates a full, half, offset, or aligned section view through the design.

Select a parent view, specify the start point of the section line, specify addition points to define the section line, then place the section view.

name: Simple Section View
tooltip:
Generates a simple (single segment cutting plane) section view from a drawing view.

Select a parent view, then specify the section line's start and end points, and then specify the insertion point for your section view.

name: Aligned Dimension
tooltip: Measures the precise distance between two points. Create dimensions that are parallel to the locations or objects that you specify.

name: Angular Dimension
tooltip: Measures the angle of a rounded edge or the angle between two points or edges.

name: Arc Length Dimension
tooltip:
Measures the distance along an arc or a polyline arc segment.

Specify arc length dimension location, or right-click to select Full/Partial arc length from the context menu, then place the dimension.

name: Arrange Dimensions
tooltip:
Arranges linear or angular dimensions.

Select a base dimension, then select dimensions to stack or align with the base dimension.

name: Auto Dimension
tooltip:
Creates dimensions automatically.

Select a dimensioning method, modify number of dimensions, datum point, and select alternate dimensions.

name: Baseline Dimension
tooltip:
Select an existing linear dimension, then specify a point to create a new dimension.

Continue specifying points to create multiple dimensions all originating from the same base point.

name: Chain Dimension
tooltip:
Select an existing linear dimension, then specify a point to create a new dimension.

Continue specifying points to create multiple side-by-side dimensions.

name: Curve Min Max Dimension
tooltip:
Measures the minimum or maximum distance from edge to curve or curve to curve.

For curve selection, start point reference for minimum and maximum distance is based on where you click on the curve.

Select Curve X/Y Min/Max snap points to measure the overall length of the curve horizontally or vertically.

name: Diameter Dimension
tooltip: Select a rounded edge, such as a fillet, hole, sphere, or cylinder, then place the dimension.

name: Dimension
tooltip:
Creates linear, aligned, angular, radius, and diameter dimensions.

Select objects, points, edges, existing dimensions, or select two points. Then place the dimension. The most appropriate dimension type is created.

name: Dimension Break
tooltip: Select existing dimensions or leaders, then add or remove breaks where they overlap other dimensions and leaders.

name: Flip Arrows
tooltip: Flips the direction of the selected dimension arrow.

name: Jogged Radial Dimension
tooltip:
Creates a radius dimension of a circle, arc or polyline arc segment with the origin of the dimension and a jog at convenient locations.

Specify the override location of the center, specify the location of the dimension line and specify the location of the jog, then place the dimension.

name: Linear Dimension
tooltip: Measures the horizontal or vertical distance between two points. Create dimensions by selecting an edge or by selecting two points.

name: Match Dimension
tooltip:
Match Dimension Configurations.

After selecting the source dimension with the configuration you want, select all the dimensions you want to apply the same configurations to.

name: Ordinate Dimension
tooltip: Define view origins and place ordinate dimensions referencing them.

name: Radius Dimension
tooltip: Select a rounded edge, such as a fillet, hole, sphere, or cylinder, then place the dimension.

name: Replace with Configured Aspect
tooltip:
Filter by Placed Configuration Tables

Filters the list to aspects from configuration tables placed in the drawing (any sheet). If none are placed, the list shows all aspects from the design configuration table.

name: Tidy Up
tooltip: Auto rearranges objects in the sheet to keep the layout tidy.

name: Export CSV
tooltip: Creates a CSV file of the selected table

name: Export DWG
tooltip: Creates a DWG file of the current drawing.

name: Export PDF
tooltip: Creates a PDF file of the current drawing.

name: Export Sheet as DXF
tooltip: Creates a DXF file of the current drawing.

name: Output Drawing Template
tooltip:
Creates a drawing template of the current drawing configuration that can be used when creating new drawings.

A template retains the current drawing's drafting standard, annotation and sheet settings, title block, and border. All drawing views, associated annotations, and parts lists are removed.

name: Finish Border
paths: Drawings Block Editor > BORDER > Finish Border

name: Finish Sketch
tooltip: Closes the sketch editing mode.
paths: Drawings Sketch Editor > SKETCH > Finish Sketch

name: Finish Sketch
paths: Drawings Sketch Editor > SKETCH > Finish Sketch

name: Finish Sketch Symbol
paths: Drawing > SKETCH SYMBOL > Finish Sketch Symbol
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Finish Sketch Symbol

name: Finish Title Block
tooltip: Closes the editor and returns to the drawing or drawing template.
paths: Drawing > TITLE BLOCK > Finish Title Block
Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Finish Title Block

name: Center Line
tooltip: Select two straight edges. The centerline is created between them.

name: Center Mark
tooltip: Select a rounded edge, such as a fillet, hole, sphere, or cylinder.

name: Center Mark Pattern
tooltip: Select rounded edges, such as holes or fillets. A center mark pattern including a PCD is created.

name: Edge Extension
tooltip: Select two straight edges. An edge extension is created for each edge that terminates at their intersection.

name: Image
tooltip: Inserts the selected image into the current block definition.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Insert
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Insert

name: Insert Image
tooltip:
Inserts an image into the current sheet.

Select an image in insert, place the image, then format as required.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Insert
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Insert

name: Insert Image
tooltip:
Inserts an image into the current sheet.

Select an image in insert, place the image, then format as required.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Insert
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Insert

name: Change Summary
tooltip: Displays a list of changes made to the reference assembly and its external references.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Inspect
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Inspect

name: History
tooltip: Shows historical records of changes, versions and revisions.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Inspect
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Inspect

name: Measure
tooltip: Reports distance, angle and positional data for the selected points.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Inspect
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Inspect

name: Copy
tooltip: Select objects to copy, specify a base point, then specify a second point to define the copy's location.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Modify
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Modify

name: Delete
tooltip: Select objects to delete, then press Enter.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Modify
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Modify

name: Extend
tooltip: Select the objects to extend. All objects automatically become extension boundaries.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Modify
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Modify

name: Move
tooltip: Select objects to move, then click Transform. Then specify a base point and a second point.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Modify
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Modify

name: Offset
tooltip: Select the object to offset, enter the offset distance, then specify a point to define to side.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Modify
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Modify

name: Refresh Properties

name: Create Sketch Symbol
tooltip: Enters Sketch mode, where you can create a sketch symbol.

name: Datum Identifier
tooltip:
Creates a datum identifier.

Select an edge, dimension extension line or feature control frame, place the datum identifier, then add an identifier and notes.

name: Edge Symbol
tooltip:
Creates an edge symbol.

Select an edge, specify attributes for the symbol like direction,values, or flag the symbol as majority symbol.

name: Feature Control Frame
tooltip:
Creates a feature control frame symbol.

Select an edge or dimension extension line, place the feature control frame symbol, then add characteristics, tolerances and datums.

name: Insert Sketch Symbol
tooltip:
Inserts and manages sketch symbols.

Insert, rename, edit, and delete symbols from the list of sketched symbols. You can also import them from another drawing file or a template.

name: Manage Sketch Symbols
tooltip:
Manages sketch symbols in your drawing template.

Rename, edit, and delete symbols from the list of sketched symbols. You can also import them from another drawing file or a template.

name: Surface Texture
tooltip:
Creates a surface texture symbol.

Select an edge, dimension extension line or feature control frame, place the surface texture symbol, then add type, requirements and process.

name: Taper and Slope
tooltip:
Creates a taper and slope symbol.

Select an edge, place the taper and slope symbol, then add type and slope/taper dimensions.

name: Welding
tooltip:
Creates a welding symbol.

Select an edge, place the welding symbol, then add type, size, length and contour.

name: Align Balloons
tooltip:
Aligns existing balloons and bend identifiers.

Select all balloons or bend identifiers to align, specify the first point, then specify a second point. The balloons or bend identifiers are distributed equally between the two points.

name: Balloon
tooltip:
Creates a balloon for the selected component.

Select a component's edge, then place the balloon.

name: Bend Identifier
tooltip:
Creates a bend identifier for the selected bend centerline.

Select a bend centerline. The bend identifier is automatically placed without a leader above the centerline. To add a leader, drag the note away from the centerline.

name: Bend Table
tooltip:
Creates a bend table based on a sheet metal flat pattern reference.

Select a flat pattern view, then place the bend table on the sheet. Bend identifiers are automatically added to the view.

name: Configuration Table
tooltip:
Displays Configuration Table data from Design on a sheet in a Drawing.

Add Configured Aspects like feature parameters and physical material from the Configuration Table in Design

name: Custom Table
tooltip:
Creates a custom table.

Place the table, then adjust the table direction, number of columns, number of rows, and text alignment.

name: Hole Table
tooltip:
Creates a hole table based on the origin you place in a drawing view.

Selecting the origin point in the view automatically selects the view and assigns hole identifiers within the view.

name: Parts List
tooltip: Generates a parts list of the model associated to the drawing.

name: Parts List
tooltip:
Creates a parts list based on an assembly, storyboard, component, or sheet metal component reference.

Select a view, select the structure, place the table on the sheet, then adjust table direction and columns. Balloons are automatically added to associated views.

name: Renumber
tooltip:
Renumbers existing balloons or bend identifiers and automatically updates associated parts lists and bend tables.

Specify the starting number, then select balloons or bend identifiers in the order you want them to appear in the parts list or bend table. Renumbering is applied based on the order of selection.

name: Revision Cloud
tooltip:
Creates a revision cloud shape based on multiple input points.

Select the cloud to edit the shape using the points and grips.

name: Revision History
tooltip:
Creates a revision history for the active sheet.

Click a vertex or point to place the history table. Press shift to toggle interactive flipping.

name: Revision Marker
tooltip:
Creates a revision marker at the selected location.

Double click the marker to edit the marker designation.

name: Table
tooltip:
Automatically creates a parts list with balloons, bend table with bend identifiers or custom table based on the contents of the current sheet or selected view.

Parts lists are created for component, assembly, and animation references. Bend tables are created for sheet metal flat pattern references.

name: Table Placeholder
tooltip:
Select a drawing view placeholder, then place the table. The table's type is determined by the view placeholder's reference.

Creates a parts list for single component, assembly or animation references, and a bend table for a sheet metal flat pattern references.

name: Attribute
tooltip: Specify a point then enter the attribute's prompt. When finished, click outside the text editor.
paths: Drawings Block Editor > TITLE BLOCK > Create
Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Create

name: Bend Note
tooltip:
Creates a bend note.

Select a bend centerline. Bend information within the selected bend centerline is automatically added as text without a leader above the bend centerline.

To add a leader, drag the note away from the centerline.

name: Hole and Thread Note
tooltip:
Creates a hole or thread note.

Select a hole or thread edge, then place the text. Hole and thread information within the selected edge is automatically added as text.

name: Leader Note
tooltip:
Creates a leader note.

Select an edge, place the text, then enter and format text as required.

name: Note
tooltip:
Automatically creates a hole, thread, bend or leader note.

Select an edge or bend centerline, then place the text.

For hole, thread and bend centerlines, information within the selected edge or bend centerline is automatically added as text.

For all other edges, enter and format text as required.

name: Text
tooltip:
Creates a note.

Specify opposing corners of the text box, then enter and format text as required.

name: Layer Stack View
tooltip:
Creates a view based on the PCB Layer Stack. Shows all layers of PCB and via pairs in abstract view.

Place the view on the sheet. Can be used in combination with Layer Stack Table.

name: Layer Stack Table
tooltip:
Creates a table based on the PCB Layer Stack.

Select between Layer Stack and Via Pairs, name the table, then adjust table columns. Leader lines are automatically added to associated diagram.

name: Refresh
tooltip:
Updates process management data in the current view.

The process management data you see can become out of date if someone else has made changes to referenced components. Use Refresh to make sure you are seeing the latest data.

name: 2-Point Rectangle
tooltip:
Creates a rectangle using 2 diagonal points.

Specify the rectangle's start point, then specify a second point to define its width and height.

tooltip:

name: Center Radius Circle
tooltip:
Creates a circle using its center point and radius.

Specify the circle's center point, then specify a second point to define its radius.

Drawings Sketch Symbol Editor > SKETCH SYMBOL > Create

name: Ellipse
tooltip:
Creates an ellipse defined by a center point, major axis and a point on the ellipse.

Select the center point of the ellipse. Select the second point to define the first axis. Select the third point to define a point on the ellipse.

tooltip: Creates numeric, alphabetic and custom labels. Specify the type, font and other properties of the label.

tooltip:

Customize the size and shape of connector obstacles by adjusting the shaft length and diameter, and clearance for bolt heads, nuts, and tooling.

name: Background Canvas
tooltip:
Places an image in the 3D space. The image will be placed in the center of current view and is oriented relative to the active camera.

Select an image to import then position and scale the image.

name: Add Package
tooltip:
Adds a package to the component.

This command attaches a package to the component to create a variant.

name: Add Package from Web
tooltip:
Opens a dialog to search for packages from library.io.

This command attaches a package to the component to create a variant.

name: Add Symbol
tooltip:
Adds a symbol to a component.

This command fetches a symbol to insert into the component.

name: Attribute
tooltip:
Definition of part attributes and their display.

An attribute is a combination of a name and a value that can specify any kind of information for a given part.

name: Name
tooltip:
Displays and optionally edits names.

Parts, elements, pads, SMDs, pins and gates can also be selected by their name, which is especially useful if the object is outside the currently shown window area. Other object types (e.g. nets, buses, signals) have to be clicked first.

name: Delete
tooltip:
Deletes selected objects.

Parts, pads, SMDs, pins and gates can also be selected by their name, which is especially useful if the object is outside the currently shown window area. Note that when selecting a multi-gate part in a schematic by name, you will need to enter the full instance name, consisting of part and gate name.

name: Change
tooltip:
Changes parameters.

The Change command is used to change or preset object properties. Select the desired parameter and value from the Change menu, or enter it from the keyboard.

name: Move
tooltip:
Moves selected objects.

Parts, pads, SMDs, pins and gates can also be selected by their name, which is especially useful if the object is outside the current window area. Note that when selecting a multi-gate part in a schematic by name, you will need to enter the full instance name, consisting of part and gate name.

name: Cross Selection
tooltip: Enable to synchronize selections across schematic and 2D PCB. Selecting an item in one view automatically selects the corresponding item in the other.

name: Polygon Selection
tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a polygon selection area.

A clockwise boundary shape selects all objects within the boundary. A counterclockwise boundary shape selects all visible objects crossed by the boundary.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

name: Select
tooltip:
Selection is always active and the active selection mode displays here.

Hold Ctrl (Windows) or Command (MacOS) to add objects to or remove objects from the selection. Change the active selection mode by selecting the mode you want to work with from the menu. Use the selection mode and selection filters to fine tune selection.

name: Window Selection
tooltip:
Selects objects enclosed in a rectangular selection area.

Click and drag from upper-left to lower-right (window selection) to select objects enclosed by the selection boundary. Click and drag from lower-right to upper-left (crossing selection) to select all visible objects the selection boundary intersects and encloses.

Use Selection Filters to include or exclude objects by type.

name: Info
tooltip:
Displays and modifies object properties.

An object's properties are displayed in a dialog, where they can be modified.

name: Show
tooltip:
Highlights objects.

Highlight complete signals and nets with the Show command. Select parts in Design Manager or enter names on the command line in format @ (example: @ FB2 FB4). If a bus is selected, all nets belonging to that bus are also highlighted.

name: Arc
tooltip:
Draw an arc of variable diameter, width, and length.

The first click defines a point on a circle, the second its diameter. Right-click to change the direction from first to second point.

name: Circle
tooltip:
Adds a circle to a drawing.

The Line Width parameter defines the width of the circle's line and is the same parameter used in the Line command.

name: Dimension
tooltip:
Adds dimensioning to a drawing.

If an object is first selected, a dimension is applied, such as the length of a straight wire, or diameter of a hole. If no object is selected, the current dimension type is added; right-click to cycle through the various types.

name: Polygon Cutout
tooltip:
Create a polygon cutout.

Polygon cutout on a routing layer will produce a void area in a polygon pour.

name: Polygon Shape
tooltip:
Create a polygon.

Polygon is a simple non-signal solid polygon shape on any layer.

name: Rectangle
tooltip:
Adds rectangles to a drawing.

Two points define two diagonally opposite corners of the rectangle.

name: Attach Existing 3D Model
tooltip:
Attaches a 3D model from your Hub or a local STEP file to the footprint.

Creates a new package from the selected geometry.

name: Copy
tooltip:
Copies objects.

Copies objects within the same drawing, or between libraries. The system generates a new name for the copy but retains the old value. When copying signals (wires), buses, and nets the names are retained, but in all other cases a new name is assigned.

name: Paste
tooltip:
Attaches a copy of the clipboard contents to the cursor, left click places the content at the cursor location on the specified layer.

Use Group, Copy, Cut, and Paste to add or subtract elements to or from your design, design block, or library component. Use right click to rotate the contents, in 90 degree increments, before placing it.

name: Flip Board
tooltip:
View opposite side of board.

The board is rotated 180 degrees around the Y axis, in model space, to look at the opposite side.

name: Single Layer View
tooltip:
Switches betwen displaying all board layers and only the active layer.

Useful when routing a dense design.

name: Align
tooltip:
Aligns selected objects.

You can align objects in relation to one another or move their origin to a nearby grid point.

name: Arrange
tooltip:
Positions selected objects in a linear or circular formation.

Select the objects to arrange. Specify the formation type, the X and Y spacing for rectangular or angular spacing for circular, and the start point. Click OK.

name: Copy Format
tooltip:
Transfers selected properties of an object to other objects of the same type.

Select the properties you want to transfer to other objects of the same type in the Select properties dialog of the selected object, then close the dialog with OK, and click the target objects.

name: Flip
tooltip:
Rotates components and objects along their X-axis and places them on the opposite side of a double-sided PCB.

Choose to reroute, disconnect, or unroute the electrical connections.

name: Mirror
tooltip:
Rotates symbols, objects, and text along their Y-axis and repositions them as a mirror of the original placement.

Use Mirror to simplify the design while you avoid crossing nets.

name: Optimize
tooltip:
Joins wire segments.

This command joins wire segments that lie in a straight line. The individual segments must be on the same layer and have the same width. This command is useful to reduce the number of objects in a drawing and to facilitate moving a complete track instead of individual segments.

name: Rotate
tooltip:
Rotates objects.

Use this command to change the orientation of objects.

name: Hole (NPTH)
tooltip:
Adds a non-plated hole to the 2D PCB.

Specify the drill parameter, indicating the hole diameter, then click to place a hole at a grid point.

name: Insert DXF/DWG
tooltip:
Browse to and select a DXF or DWG file.

Specify the desired insert values. To explicitly place the file, use Placement Origin. To implicitly place the file, click the location in the canvas.

name: Insert SVG
tooltip:
Browse to and select an SVG file.

Specify the desired insert values. To explicitly place the file, use Placement Origin. To implicitly place the file, click the location in the canvas.

name: Line
tooltip:
Adds lines (tracks) to a drawing.

The line begins at the first point specified and runs to the second. Additional points draw additional line segments. Two mouse clicks at the same position finish the line, and a new one can be started at the position of the next mouse click.

name: PTH Pad
tooltip:
Adds Plated Through-Hole (PTH) pads on a footprint.

PTH Pad dialog adjusts pad properties such as Rotate, PadShape, and Dimensions. Pads can be placed in the footprint area and are named sequentially based on their placement.

name: PTH Pad Array
tooltip:
Adds a series of PTH pads on a footprint.

Enter a Base Name, pick pad sides, select a shape, set pad numbers and start index. Add a border with >NAME and >VALUE labels and adjusts pad spacing in X and Y directions. Selecting OK places the pads.

name: Pattern
tooltip:
Makes multiple instances of the selected object(s) and places them in a linear or circular formation.

Select the objects to pattern. Specify the number of instances in the pattern, the X and Y spacing for rectangular, or angular spacing for circular patterns, and the start point for the pattern. Click OK .

name: SMD Pad
tooltip:
Adds Surface Mount Device (SMD) pads on a footprint.

SMD Pad dialog adjusts pad properties such as Angle, Size, and Roundness. Pads can be placed in the footprint area and are named sequentially based on their placement.

name: SMD Pad Array
tooltip:
Adds a series of SMD pads on a footprint.

Enter a Base Name, pick pad sides, select a shape, set pad numbers and start index. Add a border with >NAME and >VALUE labels and adjusts pad spacing in X and Y directions. Selecting OK places the pads.

name: Text
tooltip:
Adds text to a drawing.

When entering several texts it is not necessary to invoke the command each time, as the text command remains active after placing text with the mouse.

name: Miter
tooltip:
Miters wire joints.

Use this command to take the edge off a point where two wires join. The two wires must be on the the same layer, and must have the same width and wire style.

name: Split
tooltip:
Splits wires and polygon edges, adding new segments.

Split a wire, segment, or polygon edge into two segments in order, for example, to introduce a bend. Split wires into parts that can be moved with the mouse during the Split command.

name: Grid Settings
tooltip:
Provides controls for defining the drawing grid.

Set grid display on/off, display style, and size.

name: Paste Pins
tooltip:
Creates pins using data copied to the clipboard from an external source.

Copy pin data from a datasheet, spreadsheet, or text file and then paste it into the current document.

name: Pin
tooltip:
Adds a Pin into an integrated circuit (IC) or chip symbol.

Pins on symbols establish the connectivity. Each pin can have unique properties during placement.

name: Pin Array
tooltip:
Adds a series of Pins into an IC or chip symbol.

Pin Arrays establish connectivity on symbols. Arrays can be personalized with a Base Name, selected placement sides, and distinct pin numbers and starting index. Including a rectangular outline and >NAME and >VALUE labels are optional.

name: Import Library
tooltip: Imports library files to Fusion (.IntLib, .SchLib, .PcbLib, .kicad_sym, and .kicad_mod).

name: Display Layers
tooltip:
Control the display of drawing layers, showing all, used layers, or unused layers.

Use the eye icon beside a layer to turn it on or off. Double-click a layer to review or modify its properties.

name: Next Layer
tooltip:
Switch to the next available layer.

Cycles through layers in sequence order, skipping hidden or unavailable layers.

name: Previous Layer
tooltip:
Switch to the previous available layer.

Cycles through layers in reverse sequence order, skipping hidden or unavailable layers.

name: Link to managed library on library.io
Pull changes from managed library on library.io
Push changes to managed library on library.io
Unlink from managed library on library.io
Run Script
tooltip:
Executes the commands in a script file.

Use this command to execute sequences of commands that are stored in a script file.

name: Run ULP
tooltip:
Executes a User Language Program from the library.

The Run command starts the User Language Program from the file 'file_name'.

name: PCB Profile
tooltip:
Define the shape of the PCB via a sketched profile.

Select a profile and an origin point.

name: Finish PCB
tooltip: Return to the Model workspace.

name: Copy EAGLE Profile
tooltip: Copies the profile supplied from EAGLE to an upstream Fusion sketch.

name: Edit EAGLE Profile
tooltip: Edit the sketch generated from EAGLE board.

name: Move PCB Components
tooltip:
Move PCB components to new locations on the board.

Select a component and move it by dragging or typing in values.

name: PCB Status
tooltip:
Check the status of the PCB shape and component positions.

Both the board shape and the component positions can be driven by either Fusion or EAGLE. Use this command to understand the state of the model.

name: Angular Global Load
tooltip:
Applies an angular velocity and/or acceleration to a generative model.

Use this load to simulate centrifugal and tangential forces like those in a spinning wheel. Select faces, edges, or vertices on the preserve geometries to define the load settings.

name: Linear Global Load
tooltip:
Applies a linear acceleration to a generative model.

Use this load to simulate a force acting on a mass experiencing linear acceleration (speed increasing) or deceleration (speed decreasing). Select faces or edges on the preserve geometries to define the load settings.

name: Load Case Attributes
tooltip:
Shows the location, magnitude, and direction of all Items in the study load case, in one place, for easy access.

Where applicable, the load case includes the loads, constraints, and gravity settings that you define.

name: Point Mass (Manual)
tooltip:
Applies a point mass load to the selected geometry.

Use the point mass to simulate the effects of an external component attached to the generative model.

Select the preserve geometry to which the component is attached and then specify a mass value.

name: Structural Constraints
tooltip:
Applies fixed, pin, or frictionless constraints to the selected geometry.

Use constraints to define interfaces between your design and the surrounding environment. You can apply constraints to multiple objects. Depending on the constraint type, you can apply them to faces, edges, or vertices.

name: Structural Loads
tooltip:
Applies structural loads to the selected geometry.

Use loads to simulate pushing, pulling, and twisting forces that your design should withstand. You can apply loads to multiple objects. Depending on the load type, you can select faces, edges, or vertices.

name: Manufacturing
tooltip:
Specifies the manufacturing constraints for the design process.

Select at least one method and specify its constraints. Each method generates additional outcomes, which you can compare to identify the optimal one for manufacturing.

name: Objectives
tooltip:
Specifies the optimization objectives and limits that the outcomes should satisfy.

You can specify the Safety Factor for the objectives. For the Maximize Stiffness objective, you can also specify the Mass Target.

name: Fluid Preserve Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns a preserve geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign a preserve geometry to incorporate bodies in the final shape of the design. These bodies don't change during the generation of outcomes. They display in green on the canvas.

name: Fluid Starting Shape
tooltip:
Assigns a starting shape to the selected body.

Assign a starting shape to treat a body as the initial shape from which the application generates an outcome(s). Using a starting shape is recommended. The body displays in yellow on the canvas.

name: Obstacle Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns an obstacle geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign an obstacle geometry to bodies that represent empty spaces where material isn't placed during the generation of outcomes. These bodies display in red on the canvas.

name: Obstacle Offset
tooltip:
Applies an obstacle offset to the selected body or bodies.

Use offsets to increase the size of obstacle geometry bodies without modifying the model geometry. You can apply one offset to a body.

name: Preserve Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns a preserve geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign a preserve geometry to incorporate bodies in the final shape of the design. These bodies don't change during the generation of outcomes. They display in green on the canvas.

name: Solid Obstacle Geometry
tooltip:
Assigns an obstacle geometry to the selected body or bodies.

Assign an obstacle geometry to bodies that represent empty spaces where fluid is not placed during the generation of an outcome(s). These bodies display in red on the canvas.

name: Solid Obstacle Offset
tooltip:
Applies an obstacle offset to the selected body or bodies.

Use offsets to increase the size of obstacle geometry bodies without modifying the model geometry. You can apply one offset to a body.

name: Starting Shape
tooltip:
Assigns a starting shape to the selected body.

Assign a starting shape to treat a body as the initial shape from which the application generates outcomes. A starting shape is optional. The body displays in yellow on the canvas.

name: Symmetry Plane
tooltip:
Defines a symmetry plane to generate symmetrical outcomes.

Select a construction plane to define it as the symmetry plane. You can define one or more symmetry planes. It requires preserve and obstacle geometries to be symmetrical about the plane(s).

name: Edit Model
tooltip:
Edits a generative model.

It enables you to create bodies to represent preserve, obstacle, and starting shape geometries in a design problem. You don’t have to create them in the original design.

name: Edit Model
tooltip:
Edits a generative model.

It enables you to create bodies to represent preserve, obstacle, and starting shape geometries in a design problem. You don’t have to create them in the original design.

name: Explore Generative Results
tooltip:
Explores design alternatives, called outcomes, using tools that help you identify the optimal outcome.

Use different views to visually explore outcomes and examine their properties. Apply filters and compare multiple outcomes. Explore an outcome in detail in the 3D view and select an outcome iteration.

name: Explore Generative Results
tooltip:
Explores design alternatives, called outcomes, using tools that help you identify the optimal outcome.

Use different views to visually explore outcomes and examine their properties. Apply filters and compare multiple outcomes. Explore an outcome in detail in the 3D view and select an outcome iteration.

name: Generate
tooltip:
Generates outcomes that satisfy the design requirements specified in the generative study.

You can select one or more studies in your design. Track the processing status in the Job Status dialog.

name: Generate
tooltip:
Generates outcomes that satisfy the design requirements specified in the generative study.

You can select one or more studies in your project. Track the processing status in the Job Status dialog.

name: Generate Details
tooltip:
Displays information about the generation of outcomes for one or more studies.

Available information includes the outcome generation status. You can save this information to a log file.

name: Job Status
tooltip:
Displays a list of all the generative jobs that have completed, or are in progress, in all your open documents.

Track the processing status of each generative job, view outcomes, and open designs for the successfully completed jobs.

You can cancel a generative job before one iteration of any outcome is generated.

name: Pre-check
tooltip:
Checks the active generative study to ensure the setup meets the requirements to generate outcomes. The icon changes color according to the study status.

Red
You can't generate outcomes because the study setup doesn’t meet some requirements. For example, there is less than the minimum number of preserve geometries or a material is missing.

Orange
You can generate outcomes, but there are potential issues with the study. For example, a preserve, obstacle, or starting shape body is missing, but the study includes the minimum number of preserve geometries.

Green
The study setup meets the requirements.

name: Previewer
tooltip:
Generates an outcome preview based on the study setup before you run a job.

Use Previewer to see how the setup affects outcomes. Then adjust the setup, if needed. Previewer ignores manufacturing and material settings. It generates the preview after Pre-check verifies that the study is ready to generate.

name: History
tooltip:
Displays the version history of the selected component.

Select a component to view its version history and optionally choose a different version.
