Converts unrouted connections into routed wires (tracks).

This command activates the manual router, which converts airwires (unrouted connections) into real wires.

name: Route Multiple
tooltip:
Converts multiple unrouted connections into routed wires (tracks).

This command activates the manual router, which converts multiple airwires (unrouted connections) into real wires.

name: Via
tooltip:
Adds vias to a board.

When the Via command is active, a via symbol is attached to the cursor. Click to place a via at the current position.

name: Via Stitching
tooltip:
Adds Via Stitching to a board.

Adjust settings like offset, spacing, pattern, and via sizes. Click OK to apply Via Stitching. Draw a Polygon to target a specific area, if not covering the entire board.

name: Push to 3D PCB
tooltip:
Syncs changes from 2D PCB to 3D PCB. If no 3D PCB is linked, creates a new 3D PCB document. Provides preferences for object visibility and fidelity in the 3D PCB document.

Select the 2D PCB objects you want in the 3D PCB. Components without 3D models are identified and represented by rectangular shapes if you include them.

name: Unroute
tooltip:
Converts routed wires and vias into unrouted signals, and changes polygons to outlines.

Choose an unroute method to control which wires are affected.

name: Unroute All
tooltip: Converts all wire segments and vias to unrouted signals.

name: Unroute Incomplete
tooltip: Converts all stubs and incomplete segments to unrouted signals.

name: Hide All PCB Sketches
tooltip:
Hide All PCB Sketches

Conceals all visible PCB sketches.

name: Net Class and Signal Colors
tooltip: Displays custom net class and signal colors to make them easier to differentiate. Press Shift+A to show or hide colors in the canvas. Customize appearance in the Inspector or Properties panel.

name: Show All PCB Sketches
tooltip:
Show All PCB Sketches

Makes all hidden PCB sketches visible.

name: Bottom Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers on the bottom layer.
where: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
paths: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > DOCUMENT > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Rules > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Manufacturing > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > SIMULATION > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > UTILITIES > VIEW > PCB Origins

name: Top Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers on the top layer.
where: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
paths: PCB Editor > DESIGN > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > DOCUMENT > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Rules > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > Manufacturing > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > SIMULATION > VIEW > PCB Origins
PCB Editor > UTILITIES > VIEW > PCB Origins

name: Mark Local Origin
tooltip:
Defines a mark on the drawing area.

The X and Y coordinates of the mouse cursor relative to that point are displayed above the canvas, with an R prefix, polar coordinates with P prefix. This command is useful when defining locations of components or cutouts. Enter MARK; to turn the mark off.

name: Export Gerber, NC Drill, Assembly and Drawing Outputs
tooltip:
Generate Gerber, NC Drill, Assembly and Drawing outputs and save the ZIP output file in current directory.

The outputs generation will use the best matching CAMJOB template based on the design's number of signal (copper) layers.

name: Export ODB++ Output
tooltip:
Generate ODB++ output and save it to the specified compressed output file (default = ZIP).

The ODB++ output generation will use any valid CAMJOB file that includes ODB++ output configuration and resides in the ODB++ output directory. If there is no such CAMJOB file in the output directory the best matching CAMJOB template based on the design's number of copper layers will be used instead.

name: Design Preferences
tooltip:
Edits parameters that drive design geometry.

Preferences include Layer Stack, Annular Ring, Pad/SMD Shapes, Thermal Isolation, and Masks. Adjusting these settings automatically calculates PCB geometries according to preferences.

name: Check Design Rules
tooltip:
Checks design rules.

Errors, if detected, are displayed in the Errors panel. Real-time rule checking can be enabled in the application settings for instant error detection.

name: Design Rules
tooltip:
Creates and edits design rules.

Design rules are evaluated each time rules are checked. Can load design rule presets from external sources and scope design rules to defined parameters.

name: Analyze Signal
tooltip:
Calculates signal integrity for a selected signal. Returns impedance, propagation delay and other values for each segment of the signal path in tabular and graphical form.

Define the frequency and target impedance range to flag and identify impedance issues to resolve in the circuit design.

name: Export PCB Data for Ansys
tooltip:
Exports PCB data to Ansys Electronics Desktop.

Specify the exported file location and the file type. Hand the file off to the Ansys Electronics Desktop.

name: Capture Image...
tooltip:
Captures the current canvas as an image.

Set the image size and resolution then set the file type (*.png, *.jpg, *.tiff) and file name.

name: Render
tooltip:
Creates a high-quality rendered image of your scene using cloud or local background rendering technology.

Choose the desired image size, settings, cloud or local render, and click Render to start the rendering process. Finished renderings will appear in your Rendering Gallery.

name: Light
tooltip:
Adds light to control illumination, shadows, and highlights in your render.

Combine scene lights with environment lighting in Scene Settings for realistic results. You can add up to eight lights per design.

name: Scene Settings
tooltip: Set the environment and lighting for the scene. This setting only affects the Rendering workspace.

name: Texture Map Controls
tooltip:
Sets the orientation of the texture applied to the body or component.

Select the object to modify then the Projection Type and the Axis. Modify the Mapping Transform using the manipulator or fields in the dialog.

name: Add Bus
tooltip:
Draws buses on the bus layer of a schematic.

A Bus is a collection of nets. A Bus has a specification and is drawn as one or more bus line segments. The bus specification can include a unique alias, which is a short name used to identify the bus.

name: Break Out Bus
tooltip:
Breaks out a single, selected, or all nets as new wires extending from a bus.

Automatically add wires with net labels extending from a bus, saving time, and reducing errors.

name: Break Out Pins
tooltip:
Breaks out all or a selection of pins from the part by extending nets a short distance from the pins.

New nets connected to pins are drawn and can be automatically named and labeled.

name: Junction
tooltip:
Places a dot at intersecting nets.

A connection dot is placed at the intersection of nets to be connected. Junctions can be placed only on nets. If placed on the intersection of different nets, the user is given the option to connect the nets.

name: Label
tooltip:
Attaches text labels to buses and nets.

Bus or net names can be placed on a schematic in any location. Click the bus or net with the mouse, and the relevant label attaches to the mouse cursor. It can be rotated (right click), and moved to a different location or layer. The second mouse click defines the location of the label.

name: Module
tooltip:
Module

Creates a module, and adds it to a new sheet.

name: Net
tooltip:
Draw nets and mark pins as No Connection (NC) on a schematic.

Draw individual connections (nets) on the Net layer of a schematic drawing. Click once to start a net and again to end a segment. Double-click the same point to finish the net. Or, mark pins as No Connection (NC).

name: Net Breakout
tooltip:
Breaks out nets from any pin of a component in the schematic.

Automatically add wires with nets assigned to devices like microcontrollers and RAM, to save time and reduce net connectivity errors. You can use auto-increment and custom label formatting options.

name: Port
tooltip:
Adds ports to modules.

Use this command to add ports to modules used in hierarchical schematics.

name: Add Custom 3D Model
tooltip:
Assigns a custom 3D model to a part or element in a schematic or board.

Existing references to a 3D model are replaced by the new package.

name: Edit Custom 3D Model
tooltip:
Edits the 3D model associated with a part or element in a schematic or board.

When a custom 3D model is associated, edits the custom 3D model instead of the originally managed 3D model.

name: Remove Custom 3D Model
tooltip:
Removes a custom 3D model override from an element or part.

The originally assigned 3D model reference is restored when you remove the override.

name: Gate Swap
tooltip:
Swaps equivalent gates on a schematic.

Both gates must be identical with the same number of pins and the same Swaplevel in the device definition, but they need not be in the same device.

name: Invoke
tooltip:
Calls a specific symbol from a device.

Select a particular gate from a device already in use and place it in the schematic (example: a power symbol with Addlevel = Request).

name: Pin Swap
tooltip:
Swaps pins or pads.

Use this command to swap pins within the same symbol that have the same swaplevel (> 0). If a board is tied to a schematic via Back Annotation, two pads can only be swapped if the related pins are swappable.

name: Renumber Designators
tooltip:
Renumbers selected reference names based on preset options.

The table will preview the proposed updates.

name: Replace
tooltip:
Replaces a component with another.

Use this command to replace a schematic component with a different component (even from a different library). The old and new device must be compatible, in that their used gates and connected pins/pads must match, either by their names or their coordinates.

name: Value
tooltip:
Displays and changes values.

Assign values to circuit elements, such as '1k' for a resistor.

name: Insert Design Block
tooltip:
Inserts a previously saved design block (.dbl) in the canvas of the active Schematic.

If a 2D PCB is associated with the inserted design block the components are positioned at the bottom left of the PCB. Switch to the 2D PCB to reposition the components.

name: Insert Electronic Design
tooltip:
Inserts a previously saved project in the canvas of the active Schematic.

If a 2D PCB is associated with the inserted project the components are positioned at the bottom left of the PCB. Switch to the 2D PCB to reposition the components.

name: Insert Schematic
tooltip: Inserts a previously saved schematic in the canvas of the active Schematic.

name: Place Components
tooltip:
Adds elements to a drawing.

This command will toggle a panel that can be used to place components onto a schematic, or footprints onto a board.

name: Slice
tooltip:
Rips up short trace segments or longer segments to left or right.

Separate multiple board traces or schematic nets for rerouting. The width defines how much of the line is ripped up by the slice. Left or right options can be selected to rip up longer segments.

name: 3D PCB
tooltip: Switches to a 3D Model of the 2D PCB that can be inserted into a mechanical assembly. If no 3D PCB exists, creates 3D PCB.

name: Schematic Origins
tooltip: Show or hide component origin markers in the schematic.

name: Document Attributes
tooltip:
Manages document-level attributes.

Add, modify, or delete document-level attributes, such as author or project identification number. Use the Text command to place the attribute string in the canvas.

name: Import Design
tooltip: Imports Altium and KiCad design files to Fusion (.PrjPcb, .SchDoc, .PcbDoc, .kicad_pro, .kicad_sch, .kicad_pcb).

name: Export Libraries
tooltip:
Exports libraries to allow you to make individual changes to components in a project.

Use to generate one or more libraries containing the selected components. Make your changes in the libraries and then use UPDATE to display the changes in the schematic or board.

name: Update design from all libraries used in design
ERC
tooltip:
Electrical Rules Check.

Use this command to test schematics for electrical errors. If a board file is loaded, the ERC command also runs a consistency check between schematic and board.

name: Net Class
tooltip:
Creates Net Classes and adds nets to them.

Net Classes are used by Design Rules and the Design Manager for scoping and organization of signals.

name: Gap Fill
tooltip:
Fills gaps in surfaces and shells.

Improves geometry by filling gaps between selected object edges. Choose the Extend or Patch options appropriate for the gap.

name: Midsurface Shell
tooltip:
Creates a new midsurface shell from the selected body.

Select the face to midsurface.

name: Offset Shell
tooltip:
Creates a new offset shell at a given distance from the selected face.

Select the face to offset then specify the distance.

name: Shell from Surface
tooltip:
Creates a new surface shell from the surface.

Select the surface to surface shell.

name: Finish Simplify
tooltip: Click Finish Simplify to return to the Simulation workspace.

name: Finish Compare
tooltip: Exits the Compare environment and returns you to the Results environment.

name: Four Views
tooltip:
Opens four windows so you can examine the data from four different results.

Click on a window to activate it to select a different result. Compare results from the same study or from different studies.

name: Four Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to four different studies.

name: One Horizontal and Three Vertical Views
tooltip:
Opens four windows so you can examine the data from four results, one above the other three.
Click on a window to activate it to select a different result. Compare results from the same study or from different studies.

name: One Horizontal and Three Vertical Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to four different studies.

name: One Horizontal and Two Vertical Views
tooltip:
Opens three windows so you can examine the data from three results, one above the other two.
Click on a window to activate it to select a different result. Compare results from the same study or from different studies.

name: One Horizontal and Two Vertical Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to three different studies.

name: One Vertical and Three Horizontal Views
tooltip:
Opens four windows so you can examine the data from four results, one to the left of the other three.
Click on a window to activate it to select a different result. Compare results from the same study or from different studies.

name: One Vertical and Three Horizontal Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to four different studies.

name: One Vertical and Two Horizontal Views
tooltip:
Opens three windows so you can examine the data from three results, one to the left of the other two.
Click on a window to activate it to select a different result. Compare results from the same study or from different studies.

name: One Vertical and Two Horizontal Views
tooltip: Compare results views from up to three different studies.

name: Two Horizontal Views
tooltip:
Opens two windows so you can compare the data from two different results, one above the other.

Click on a window to activate it to select a different result. Compare results from the same study or from different studies.

name: Two Horizontal Views
tooltip: Compare results views from one or two different studies.

name: Two Vertical Views
tooltip:
Opens two windows so you can compare the data from two different results, side-by-side.

Click on a window to activate it to select a different result. Compare results from the same study or from different studies.

name: Two Vertical Views
tooltip: Compare results views from one or two different studies.

name: Synchronize Animations
tooltip:
Synchronizes the animation controls so that all animated results move to the next frame, stop, pause, and loop at the same time.

This command activates automatically if the active result is an animated result when you enter Compare. Deactivate the command to control animations independently.

name: Synchronize Cameras
tooltip:
Synchronizes the movement and orientation of the models in all windows, based on the active window, so you can move, rotate, zoom in or out, and pan all models in the same way and at the same time.

Click Synchronize Cameras to deactivate it, when you want to manipulate the models independently.

name: Synchronize Legends
tooltip:
Synchronizes the legend range for all results of the same type, so you can compare the results more effectively.

On by default, this command also changes the result settings and legend behavior in all non-active windows to match the behavior in the active window. Deactivate to manipulate the legends independently.

name: Synchronize Result Types
tooltip:
Synchronizes the result selection so that all windows show the same result type as the active window.

On by default, this command only synchronizes results from the same study type. Deactivate to view different results from the same study, or across different study types.

name: Convergence Plot
tooltip:
Shows how the data changes at each iterative step as the mesh element size is decreased.

This plot is generated when you enable adaptive mesh refinement before you solve.

name: Compare
tooltip:
Enters Compare mode. Setup comparisons and access results of multiple simulations simultaneously. View results from different studies side by side.

Select Finish Compare to exit out of the mode.

name: Actual
tooltip:
The actual deformation may be so small that the model shape is unaltered. To view the deformed shape, select a scaling option.

Undeformed: Displays original model shape
Actual: Displays the computed deformation.
Use these options to display the maximum deformation as a percentage of the model size:
Adjusted 0.5x: 2.5%
Adjusted: 5%
Adjusted 2x: 10%
Adjusted 5x: 25%

name: Actual
tooltip:
Displays the calculated deformation.

The actual deformation is often too small to see. Actual is the default for Nonlinear Static Stress and Event Simulation studies where large displacements are expected.

name: Adjusted
tooltip:
The actual deformation may be so small that the model shape is unaltered. To view the deformed shape, select a scaling option.

Undeformed: Displays original model shape
Actual: Displays the computed deformation.
Use these options to display the maximum deformation as a percentage of the model size:
Adjusted 0.5x: 2.5%
Adjusted: 5%
Adjusted 2x: 10%
Adjusted 5x: 25%

name: Adjusted
tooltip:
Displays the deformation on an adjusted scale.

This is the default for all studies except Nonlinear Static Stress and Event Simulation.

name: Adjusted 0.5x
tooltip:
The actual deformation may be so small that the model shape is unaltered. To view the deformed shape, select a scaling option.

Undeformed: Displays original model shape
Actual: Displays the computed deformation.
Use these options to display the maximum deformation as a percentage of the model size:
Adjusted 0.5x: 2.5%
Adjusted: 5%
Adjusted 2x: 10%
Adjusted 5x: 25%

name: Adjusted 0.5x
tooltip:
Displays half the deformation compared to Adjusted.

Use Adjusted 0.5x when the deformation appears too large using Adjusted.

name: Adjusted 2x
tooltip:
The actual deformation may be so small that the model shape is unaltered. To view the deformed shape, select a scaling option.

Undeformed: Displays original model shape
Actual: Displays the computed deformation.
Use these options to display the maximum deformation as a percentage of the model size:
Adjusted 0.5x: 2.5%
Adjusted: 5%
Adjusted 2x: 10%
Adjusted 5x: 25%

name: Adjusted 2x
tooltip:
Displays twice the deformation compared to Adjusted.

Use Adjusted 2x when the model shape does not change enough to see where the deformation occurs.

name: Adjusted 5x
tooltip:
The actual deformation may be so small that the model shape is unaltered. To view the deformed shape, select a scaling option.

Undeformed: Displays original model shape
Actual: Displays the computed deformation.
Use these options to display the maximum deformation as a percentage of the model size:
Adjusted 0.5x: 2.5%
Adjusted: 5%
Adjusted 2x: 10%
Adjusted 5x: 25%

name: Adjusted 5x
tooltip:
Displays five times the deformation compared to Adjusted.

Use Adjusted 5x when the model shape does not change enough to see the deformation clearly.

name: Undeformed
tooltip:
The actual deformation may be so small that the model shape is unaltered. To view the deformed shape, select a scaling option.

Undeformed: Displays original model shape
Actual: Displays the computed deformation.
Use these options to display the maximum deformation as a percentage of the model size:
Adjusted 0.5x: 2.5%
Adjusted: 5%
Adjusted 2x: 10%
Adjusted 5x: 25%

name: Undeformed
tooltip: Displays the results on the undeformed model.

name: Mesh View
tooltip:
Displays the mesh as a reference over the result plot.

Check the mesh quality if you see unusual result values, such as stress. An overly coarse mesh, or unusual mesh element shapes, can lead to inaccurate results, so refine as necessary.

name: Wireframe View
tooltip: Displays the undeformed wireframe as a reference, to show how much the model deflects in response to the applied loads and constraints.

name: Finish Results
tooltip: Exits the Results environment and returns you to the Setup environment.

name: Center of Mass
tooltip: Shows both displaced and undisplaced center of mass for bodies.

name: Center of Mass
tooltip:
Lists the location of the original and displaced center of mass, and the displacement vector.

The displaced center of mass is shown on the model by a glyph.

name: Create Point Probe
tooltip: Query the result value for position in global coordinate space.

name: Create Slice Plane
tooltip: Use a slice plane to clip the result plot and see the results inside the model.

name: Create Surface Probes
tooltip: Query interactively for the result values on the mesh surface.

name: Delete All Probes
tooltip:
Removes all probes and the information associated with them.
To hide the probe information, without deleting the probes, select Hide All Probes from the toolbar Inspect panel.

name: Delete All Probes
tooltip:
Removes all probes and the information associated with them.
To hide the probe information, without deleting the probes, select Hide All Probes from the toolbar Inspect panel.

name: Hide All Probes
tooltip:
Hides all probes and the information labels associated with them.
If you no longer need the probe information, an alternative is to delete the probes, using Delete All Probes from the toolbar Inspect panel.

name: Hide All Probes
tooltip:
Hides all probes and the information labels associated with them.
If you no longer need the probe information, an alternative is to delete the probes, using Delete All Probes from the toolbar Inspect panel.

name: Reactions
tooltip: Shows resulting reaction forces and moments.

name: Reactions
tooltip:
Lists the forces and moments a constrained model generates in response to applied loads.

Use reactions to check your study setup. The sum of the reactions should be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the total applied loads.

name: Show All Probes
tooltip: Makes visible all probes that you have previously hidden, so you can see the data in their labels again.

name: Show All Probes
tooltip: Makes visible all probes that you have previously hidden, so you can see the data in their labels again.

name: Show Min/Max
tooltip: Display the location of the maximum and minimum values of the current result quantity.

name: Solver Data
tooltip: View solver information and statistics about the current study.

name: Mass Participation Factors
tooltip:
Use the Mass Participation Factor to assess the percentage of the system mass that participates per direction for each mode.
Note that modes with a large effective mass participation typically have a stronger influence on the system response.

name: Load Case Attributes
tooltip:
Shows the location, magnitude, and direction of all Items in the study load case, in one place, for easy access.

Where applicable, the load case includes the loads, constraints, and gravity settings that you define.

name: Animate
tooltip: Interpolates results values based on the loading factor (Static Stress Analysis, Thermal Stress Analysis) or based on the period of the observed mode (Modal Analysis).

name: Convergence Plot
tooltip: Monitor the progress of the simulation. Values of the active result type are displayed for each iteration as well as the convergence rate.

name: Legend Min/Max
tooltip:
Reduces the range of result values shown on the legend, while maintaining the entire spectrum of colors, to give you a more granular view of particular areas of interest on the model.

Use the legend sliders to make transparent values that are of no interest to you.

name: Legend Options
tooltip:
Customize the legend appearance.
Specify the size, color transition, and plot shading. The Legend appearance can be unique in every displayed view.

name: Mass Participation Factors
tooltip:
Use the Mass Participation Factor to assess the percentage of the system mass that participates per direction for each mode.
Note that modes with a large effective mass participation typically have a stronger influence on the system response. The compact dialog displays the mass participation for the active mode. To display all modes, expand the dialog.

name: Promote
tooltip: Converts the Shape Optimization results to a new Mesh Body. The Mesh Body can be edited using the modeling tools.

name: Solver Data
tooltip:
Displays a summary of the mesh details and solver status to help you troubleshoot your study results.

Switch to Solver Output to see the solver log, which includes solver details, time statistics, warnings, and errors.

name: Molding Process
tooltip:
Shows a log of the study data in two formats, an Overview format and a Table format.

Animate the Overview to see how the data changes with time. This view provides the data in the context of the injection molding process. Select the Table format to view all the data points from the start to the end of the simulation.

name: Export Study to Ansys® Setup
tooltip:
Export geometry, loads, constraints, and materials of the active study to Ansys Setup.

When you import the .sdz file into an Ansys product, the same study that was set up in Fusion is created automatically, although some loads and constraints may need to be recreated.

name: Send Study to Ansys® Discovery™
tooltip:
Send geometry, loads, constraints, and materials of the active study to Ansys Discovery.

The same study that was set up in Fusion is created automatically, although some loads and constraints may need to be recreated in Ansys Discovery.

name: Send Study to Ansys® Mechanical™
tooltip:
Send geometry, loads, constraints, and materials of the active study to Ansys Mechanical.

The same study that was set up in Fusion is created automatically, although some loads and constraints may need to be recreated in Ansys Mechanical.

name: Bolt Connector
tooltip:
Characterizes a bolted connection between two bodies.

Use bolt connectors to mathematically represent threaded fasteners that hold together an assembly. Avoid spending time and effort to produce, mesh, and solve solid models of fastener parts.

Specify the subtype as a nut or threaded hole bolt type of connection. You can include an optional washer at either end. Enter the size, preload and material of the bolt to ensure accurate representation of the connection.

name: Prescribed Rotation
tooltip:
Apply an angle, rotational velocity, or rotational acceleration to the model.

The constraint is applied for the duration specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Prescribed Rotation
tooltip:
Apply an angle to the model.

The constraint is applied for the steps specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Prescribed Translation
tooltip:
Apply a displacement, velocity, or acceleration to the model.

The constraint is applied for the duration specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Prescribed Translation
tooltip:
Apply a displacement to the model.

The constraint is applied for the steps specified by the multiplier curve.

name: Rigid Body Connector
tooltip:
Rigidly connect a vertex on a body to faces, edges or vertices on another body

There are two subtypes of rigid body connectors, this should be specified first. The second selection will be a vertex. The third selection can include one or more faces, edges, or vertices:

Rigid body: The first vertex selected is the Anchor Point, which is the independent vertex. The motion of the entities in the second set is dependent on the motion of the Anchor Point. The dependent entities move exactly as the independent vertex moves.

Interpolation: The first vertex you select is a Reference Point. The items in the second selection are independent entities to average. In this case, the Reference Point is the dependent entity (its motion is controlled by the motion of the independent entities). The weighted average of the displacement of the independent entitites is applied to the reference point.

name: Spring Connector
tooltip:
Provides an elastic connection between two vertices.

A spring can connect two vertices on the same part or two different parts.

name: Structural Constraints
tooltip:
Applies a fixed, pinned, frictionless, prescribed displacement or remote constraint to the selected geometry.

You can apply constraints to multiple entities you select.

name: Structural Constraints
tooltip:
Applies a fixed, pinned, or frictionless to the selected geometry.

You can apply constraints to multiple entities you select.

name: Automatic Contacts
tooltip:
Automatically calculates the contact types between all bodies and components that overlap or touch each other.

To ensure all contacts are included in the simulation, run Automatic Contacts before assigning manual contacts. Note, you can then later change the contact types from the automatically generated one to the desired type. Also, you can suppress contacts to be excluded from the simulation.

name: Global Contacts
tooltip:
Use the Global Contacts command to automatically generate contact pairs.
Contact pairs are only generated between bodies, not between faces or edges.

name: Manage Contacts
tooltip:
View the list of all contacts.

The list allows you to edit, and suppress contacts.

name: Manage Contacts
tooltip:
View the list of all contacts.

The list allows you to sort, edit, rename, suppress, and isolate contacts.

name: Manual Contacts
tooltip:
Applies contact conditions to component geometries.

After you detect all automatic contacts, you can create additional contacts between components. The simulation type determines the availability of contact types.

name: DOF View
tooltip:
Shows the degrees of freedom status for each body.

Use DOF View to identify where contacts or constraints are needed. Change the Fully Fixed color to invisible to reveal free bodies that are hard to find.

name: Groups View
tooltip:
Uses colors to show groups of connected bodies with bonded contacts.

Each group has a different color. Bodies with missing contacts, or with other types of contact, are colored gray.

name: Model View
tooltip:
Displays the model components with the original design appearances.

Select Display Study Material Colors from the Materials panel to see the material colors.

name: Angular Global Load
tooltip:
Applies an angular velocity and/or acceleration to the entire model, to represent centrifugal and tangential forces such as those experienced by a spinning wheel.

Select faces or edges to define the direction and location references of the applied load.

name: Edit Gravity
tooltip:
Modifies the magnitude and direction of the applied gravity.

Use as an alternative to realigning your model with the global coordinate system, when your model is not imported in the correct orientation.

name: Initial Angular Velocity
tooltip: Apply rotational motion to a body at the start of the analysis

name: Initial Linear Velocity
tooltip: Apply constant motion to a body at the start of the analysis.

name: Linear Global Load
tooltip:
Applies a linear acceleration to the entire model, to represent forces such as those experienced by a mass accelerating or decelerating in a straight line.

Specify the acceleration direction by selecting a face normal to the direction of the load or by specifying an angle or a vector.

name: Point Mass (Auto)
tooltip:
Use Auto Point Mass to represent the effects of an existing component in the simulation model. This is useful for simplifying the simulation model.

To assign a point mass, select the geometric item on which the point mass acts.

name: Point Mass (Manual)
tooltip:
Use Manual Point Mass to represent the effects of a component or mass not included in the simulation model. Such a component should have very little effect on the model stiffness.

After specifying the location on the model, specify its mass. Point masses are useful for reducing model complexity.

name: Structural Loads
tooltip:
Applies structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and some load types apply only to certain geometry types - for example, Moments only apply to faces.

name: Thermal Loads
tooltip:
Applies thermal loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and apply one or more thermal loads. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and you cannot combine temperature loads with the other thermal loads (heat source, radiation, or convection).

name: Toggle Gravity Off
tooltip:
Enables you to suppress the gravity load.

By default, gravity acts in the negative Y direction. A symbol at the model origin indicates the direction of gravity. To modify the gravity magnitude or direction, use the Edit Gravity command.

name: Toggle Gravity On
tooltip:
Enables you to unsuppress the gravity load.

By default, gravity acts in the negative Y direction. A symbol at the model origin indicates the direction of gravity. To modify the gravity magnitude or direction, use the Edit Gravity command.

name: Transient Loads
tooltip:
Applies transient structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and some load types apply only to certain geometry types.

name: Transient Loads
tooltip:
Applies transient structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set and some load types apply only to certain geometry types.

name: Transient Loads
tooltip:
Applies transient structural loads to selected geometry.

Individually or multi-select faces, edges, or vertices and specify the load magnitude and direction. You cannot mix geometry types in your selection set.

name: Adaptive Mesh Refinement
tooltip:
Enable and modify Adaptive Mesh Refinement.

Adaptive Mesh Refinement iteratively improves the mesh based on computed results. The goal is to reach a solution that does not change with further mesh refinement.

name: Element Deletion Criteria
tooltip:
Deletes elements from the mesh that, during the event simulation, fall into the region of emerging cracks, breaks, and holes.

Define the criteria that must be met for elements to be deleted. Select the target body, the deletion criterion, and the value. Only mesh elements of the selected body that meet the deletion criteria are deleted.

name: Load Case Attributes
tooltip:
Shows the location, magnitude, and direction of all Items in the study load case, in one place, for easy access.

Where applicable, the load case includes the loads, constraints, and gravity settings that you define.

name: Local Mesh Control
tooltip:
Refine the mesh in specific locations by modifying the mesh distribution on Faces and edges.

To improve results fidelity, strategically refine the mesh at certain locations. Refine the mesh in areas that have a large result gradient or have small geometric features that the global mesh size may not capture. Select Surfaces or edges, and drag the slider. Validate that the mesh is sufficient before running the simulation using the Generate Mesh command.

name: Settings
tooltip: Enables you to view and modify all settings for the current simulation study.

name: Display Study Material Colors
tooltip:
Colors the model according to the materials selected for the Simulation study.

When this option is not selected, the study material colors are hidden and the Design workspace material colors are shown instead.

name: Manage Physical Materials
tooltip:
Lists properties for each material in the Fusion libraries, that control the material's thermal, mechanical, and elastic behavior, as well as its appearance.

Use the Material Browser to identify favorites, modify properties, create new materials, and manage personal libraries.

name: Material Properties
tooltip: Displays material properties.

name: Study Materials
tooltip:
Compares the materials chosen for the Simulation model against those in the Design model, and enables you to change the Simulation model materials.

For accurate results, make sure you assign materials to your Simulation model that best represent the actual material that will be used for production.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip: Display model using calculated results.

name: Simulation Results
tooltip: Shows how your model performs under the study setup conditions.

name: Rigid Bodies
tooltip:
Assigns selected bodies as Rigid to reduce computational time.

Rigid Bodies are included in the analysis, but no stresses or strains are calculated for them. These parts can still move and rotate, but they won't deform.

name: Preserve Region
tooltip:
Excludes region from Shape Optimization process.

Specifies the region(s) of the model to exclude from the Shape Optimization process. Region shapes include box, cylinder, and sphere.

name: Shape Optimization Criteria
tooltip:
Specify the optimization objectives and load case constraints.

Set the target mass, objectives, manufacturing constraints, and maximum allowed displacement.

name: Symmetry Plane
tooltip:
Creates a symmetry plane.

Forces the generated shape to be symmetric about the symmetry plane(s).

name: Target Body
tooltip:
Identifies the body to optimize by the removal of surplus material, without compromising strength.

It is important to validate that the new design can withstand operational loads, using a static stress or similar study.

name: Simplify
tooltip:
Removes detailed features that are unnecessary for simulations without affecting your production geometry.

Select Finish Simplify to exit out of the mode.

name: Data Check
tooltip: Check explicit solve.

name: Generate Mesh
tooltip:
Computes a mesh for your simulation model based on settings specified. Automatic contacts are generated first.

Your computer will be used to perform the compute process.

name: Hide Meshing Issues
tooltip:
Hides meshing issues.

Meshing issues.

name: Job Status
tooltip:
Displays a list of all the studies that have solved, or are in progress, in all your open documents.

Track the progress of running jobs, cancel them, or access the results of completed studies.

name: Pre-check
tooltip:
Checks the study setup to ensure it has all the information required to solve. The icon color indicates the setup status:

Red
The Study cannot be solved because vital information is missing, such as valid material data.

Orange
The solver can run, but may produce unexpected results. Check the setup to ensure it is as you intend.

Green
The study can be solved and has no predictable issues.

name: Show Meshing Issues
tooltip:
Shows meshing issues on the model.

Meshing issues.

name: Solve
tooltip:
Solves the simulation using the study setup conditions you defined.

Run Pre-check before solving, to verify that the study setup is complete. Solve one or more studies simultaneously. Track the progress in the Job Status dialog.

name: Solve Details
tooltip:
Displays information about jobs in the active document, including whether or not they ran successfully.

Errors and warnings are also listed, with suggestions on how to resolve them. You can save this information to a log file, or share it in an e-mail.

name: Copy Study
tooltip:
Copies studies from one configuration to other configurations in the same design document.

Save time, and avoid manually creating studies for each configuration, by setting up all your study requirements for one configuration, then copying them to your other configurations automatically.

name: New Simulation Study
tooltip:
Creates a new simulation study.

Select a study type and define settings specific to this study type.

name: New Simulation Study From Generative Design
tooltip:
Creates a new Static Stress simulation study from the setup of a generative study.

The new study has the same load case attributes as the generative study. The material from the selected outcome is applied. Select the same units as for the outcome in the Explore workspace.

name: Update Simulation Study
tooltip: Update Active Simulation Study

name: Safety Factor Thresholds
tooltip:
Applies lower and upper thresholds to the result legend to show you if your model is strong enough.

Change the default values to use your industry or company standards.
